capability_investigated:
WhisperProcessor feature extraction and the batch shape that generate()
accepts: input_features is a fixed 30s (3000-frame) log-mel per call, and
generate(features, prompts) takes a stacked (N, mel, 3000) feature batch
with one prompt list per window.
what_i_learned:
The stub's single processor(audio) call hard-truncates each recording to
30 seconds — anything past the first window is never fed to the model, so
the dominant error is deletion of the entire tail, not a decode-quality
problem. Batching N stacked 30s windows through one generate() call returns
N independent result objects, one per window.
hypothesis:
Slicing the waveform into consecutive non-overlapping 30s windows and
batch-decoding all of them recovers the deleted tail; concatenating the
per-window decodes should sharply raise length_ratio and cut deletion-driven
CER versus the single-window stub.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch dimension vs. GPU memory: how many stacked (mel, 3000)
windows one generate() call can hold before CUDA OOMs.
what_i_learned:
Batching ALL 30s windows of a full 0715 call-center recording into one
generate() call exceeds float16 CUDA memory and crashes (RuntimeError: CUDA
out of memory) — the recordings are long enough (many minutes) that the
window count blows the batch. Memory scales with batch size, so decoding one
window per generate() call bounds peak memory to a single window and still
recovers the full tail.
hypothesis:
Replace the single stacked batched generate() with a sequential loop that
decodes each consecutive 30s window in its own generate() call and joins the
per-window text, eliminating the OOM while preserving long-form coverage.

capability_investigated:
The input side of the pipeline rather than a decode knob — the raw waveform
passed to transcribe() before it reaches processor(). I derived per-frame RMS
energy (20ms frames) on the numpy audio to locate speech vs. silence, an
input the pipeline had never conditioned on. The audio profiles confirm the
signal is there: silence_ratio 6–25% and single silences up to 34s per file.
what_i_learned:
Fixed 30s windowing has two deletion sources independent of decode quality:
seams land mid-utterance (token loss at every boundary), and any window
carrying a long silence feeds that silence to the decoder, which is what
drives Whisper's repetition/hallucination collapse (repeated_text 0.36 on
best). Frame-energy VAD is computable with numpy alone (no silero/backend
dependency) and lets seams fall in silence while clear silence is dropped
from what the model ever sees.
hypothesis:
Replace blind fixed windows with energy-VAD windows: compute frame RMS,
threshold at peak−40dB, merge speech across <0.5s gaps, pad 0.25s, and pack
regions into <=30s windows that break only at silence (force-splitting any
single region longer than 30s). Cutting at silence removes boundary deletions
and feeding less silence should cut the repetition collapse that deletes
whole-window content — directly attacking the coverage/deletion axis while
keeping one-window peak memory.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return tokens when timestamps are ENABLED (prompt omits
<|notimestamps|>): the sequences_ids then interleave Whisper timestamp
tokens whose id maps linearly to a time offset, (id - timestamp_begin)*0.02s.
This is the return channel every prior iteration suppressed via
<|notimestamps|> + skip_special_tokens.
what_i_learned:
With timestamps on, each 30s window's decoded token stream reports where the
model thinks speech ended (the last timestamp token), giving a model-derived
boundary independent of any waveform-energy heuristic. timestamp_begin is
recoverable from the tokenizer as convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>"), so the
whole long-form seek loop is buildable through the frozen surface alone — no
silero/VAD and no direct ctranslate2 access needed.
hypothesis:
Replace energy-VAD segmentation with timestamp-guided sequential long-form:
decode a 30s window with timestamps, advance seek to the last emitted
timestamp, emit text only up to that segment, repeat. Boundaries chosen by
the model rather than by an energy threshold should stop dropping the span
after early/mis-placed seams, directly lifting length_ratio and cutting the
68% deletion mass.

capability_investigated:
The prompts argument of generate(): whether the per-window prompt list can
carry a <|startofprev|> context prefix (prior transcript tokens) ahead of the
<|startoftranscript|>/<|ko|>/<|transcribe|> SOT sequence, and whether
generate() returns only the freshly generated tokens (leaving timestamp
parsing intact) when given such a prefix.
what_i_learned:
Every prior iteration passed generate() only the bare SOT sequence as prompt,
leaving the decoder with zero running context — so cross-window term
consistency was never exploited. Whisper's prompt channel accepts a
<|startofprev|> token (recoverable via convert_tokens_to_ids) followed by
arbitrary prior-text token ids before SOT; this is the native
condition_on_previous_text mechanism and is reachable entirely through the
frozen surface (no direct ctranslate2 access).
hypothesis:
Carry the previous window's clean emitted text (capped at 224 tokens) as a
<|startofprev|> prompt prefix for the next window's decode. Conditioning on
running context biases consistent spelling of domain terms/names across
windows, attacking the dominant substitution axis (56%) without disturbing
the timestamp-seek coverage logic that already holds length_ratio at 0.94.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_scores and return_no_speech_prob kwargs and the
corresponding result fields (res.scores[0] = hypothesis log-probability,
res.no_speech_prob). Every prior iteration called generate() with only
beam_size/sampling_temperature and read only sequences_ids — the per-window
confidence channel was never requested or inspected.
what_i_learned:
ctranslate2's WhisperGenerationResult can return scores (a log-prob
confidence per hypothesis) and no_speech_prob alongside sequences_ids when
return_scores/return_no_speech_prob are passed. This makes a per-window
quality signal available through the frozen surface alone, which is the
prerequisite for any confidence-gated retry — the greedy pass otherwise has
no way to detect it committed to a wrong path.
hypothesis:
Replace the single greedy decode per window with a confidence-gated
temperature-fallback loop (temps 0.0/0.4/0.8): decode greedily, and if
avg log-prob < -1.0 or gzip compression ratio > 2.4 the window is re-decoded
with sampling at a higher temperature, escalating until it clears the gate.
Targets the substitution-dominant axis by letting low-confidence windows
(the worst-cer and hallucination files) escape the greedy basin instead of
emitting a confidently-wrong transcript; cost is bounded since only failing
windows retry.

capability_investigated:
The semantics of the multiple timestamp tokens within a single window's
sequences_ids (not just the last one). The timestamp channel (discovered
iter_004) carries every inter-segment boundary, so token_ids[ts_positions[-2]]
gives the penultimate boundary, letting me choose how many trailing segments
to commit vs. defer to the next window's overlap.
what_i_learned:
Each 30s window's right-edge final segment is the one Whisper decodes with the
least right-context, and the timestamp channel exposes enough boundaries to
defer it: advancing seek to the penultimate timestamp (instead of the last)
re-feeds that segment as an interior, fully right-contexted segment of the next
window. The penultimate-boundary offset also bounds the re-read cost — when it
lands >=20s in, the deferred tail is short, so window count stays <=1.5x.
hypothesis:
Substitution (56%, dominant; coverage healthy at len 0.94) is partly driven by
context-starved trailing segments. Ending each window one segment early so
every segment gets at least one decode where it is not the window's right edge
should lower substitution without re-introducing deletions.

capability_investigated:
How a window decode behaves under re-decoding: pairing generate()'s
return_scores channel (res.scores[0] = hypothesis avg log-prob, found
iter_006) with sampling_temperature>0 + sampling_topk=0 to draw a DIFFERENT
token path for the same audio, rather than the one fixed greedy path every
prior iteration committed to.
what_i_learned:
The greedy single-pass decode (beam_size=1, sampling_temperature=0.0) that
every prior pipeline used has no escape hatch — a window where greedy locks
onto a wrong token path stays wrong, which matches the substitution-heavy
profile (sub 57%, length_ratio 0.94 healthy). The scores channel plus a zlib
compression ratio over the decoded text are enough to gate a decode
(avg_logprob < -1.0 = low confidence, cr > 2.4 = repetition collapse), and
sampling_topk=0 with temperature>0 actually perturbs the path (topk=1 stays
greedy regardless of temperature), making a per-window re-decode loop
reachable entirely through the frozen surface.
hypothesis:
Re-decode any window that fails the avg-logprob/compression-ratio gate at an
escalating temperature (0.0->1.0 ladder) and keep the first gate-passing
attempt (else the highest-logprob one). Clean windows pass at t=0 so cost is
bounded; low-confidence/repetition windows get a chance to escape the bad
greedy commit, lowering substitution and fixing the repeated_text guard file.

capability_investigated:
The waveform input to transcribe() before it reaches processor()/feature
extraction — specifically the absolute amplitude/loudness of the signal.
Whisper's log-mel front end normalizes only RELATIVE to each input's own
loudest frame (log_spec.max() - 8), so global/speech-level loudness is an
input the model is sensitive to but the pipeline has never conditioned on
or modified (iter_003 only measured frame RMS for VAD, never rescaled).
what_i_learned:
Per-file loudness varies enormously across the 0715 batch (rms_db_mean
-26 dB to -41 dB) and is computable+modifiable with numpy alone, no
backend/silero dependency. Because Whisper's mel normalization is only
per-input-max-relative, a globally quiet recording (or one with a few loud
bursts dominating the max) yields compressed, low-contrast mel magnitudes —
weak features that match the substitution-heavy / length-ratio-healthy
profile (confident-but-wrong char paths, not deletions). Speech level is
separable from silence by taking RMS over only the louder half of 20ms frames.
hypothesis:
Replace the decode-side temperature-fallback machinery with an input-side
loudness normalization: remove DC offset, estimate speech-level RMS over the
louder-half of frames, and scale every recording to a common target (~-20
dBFS) before feature extraction, then decode with a single clean greedy pass
plus the established timestamp seek. Consistent front-end loudness should
sharpen mel contrast on the quiet files and reduce substitutions where
coverage is already healthy.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s search-based decode channel: beam_size>1 with patience runs a
real parallel beam search (not greedy/sampled single-path), and num_hypotheses>1
makes res.sequences_ids a score-ranked K-best list rather than one hypothesis.
no_repeat_ngram_size blocks within-hypothesis loops at decode time. Every prior
iteration hard-coded beam_size=1, so none of these were ever exercised.
what_i_learned:
The backend exposes true beam search and an N-best return channel through the
frozen surface: with beam_size=K + num_hypotheses=K, res.sequences_ids returns
K hypotheses ordered by score and res.scores their log-probs — a structurally
different decode strategy from the temperature-resampling ladder (which only
draws stochastic alternate full paths under beam_size=1). Beam search selects
by GLOBAL cumulative log-prob, the direct lever for the substitution-from-bad-
-local-commit profile that resampling/greedy cannot search around.
hypothesis:
Replace the temperature-fallback ladder with one beam-search decode per window
(beam_size=5, patience=1, num_hypotheses=5, no_repeat_ngram_size=3), selecting
the highest-scoring K-best hypothesis whose decoded text clears the compression-
ratio gate. Parallel-path search should recover domain-term/phone-band
substitutions where the locally-greedy token was wrong but a globally-better
path existed in the beam.

capability_investigated:
The prompts argument of generate(): wiring the <|startofprev|> context-prefix
channel (recoverable via convert_tokens_to_ids("<|startofprev|>"), ledger
iter_005) into a full pipeline — prepending the running decoded transcript
tail ahead of the SOT sequence so each window decodes WITH prior-text context,
Whisper's native condition_on_previous_text. Every prior pipeline passed only
the bare SOT sequence, decoding each 30s window in total isolation.
what_i_learned:
The prior-text prefix is the only lever tried so far that conditions the
decode on transcript content rather than re-searching the acoustic path for a
single isolated window (iter_008 temperature ladder, iter_010 beam search both
do the latter). Because the substitution profile (sub 57%, length_ratio 0.94
healthy) is wrong-CHARACTER domain-term spellings, not coverage loss, a
language-model-context lever is acoustically orthogonal to every decode-search
knob already exhausted. Content tokens for the carried buffer are separable
from interleaved timestamp tokens by t < timestamp_begin, so the running
context is buildable from emit_ids alone without re-tokenizing decoded text.
hypothesis:
Threading the last ~224 decoded content tokens into each window's prompt as
<|startofprev|> prior text biases in-domain term spellings to stay consistent
once decoded correctly, and gives window-start tokens left-context they
previously lacked — directly lowering substitution. Decode kept single greedy
to isolate the prior-text effect from any resampling ladder.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prompt prefix (channel found iter_005) used as a STATIC
domain-glossary language prior, rather than as a running-transcript carry
(iter_011). Studied how curated, fixed content token ids placed between
<|startofprev|> and the SOT sequence bias the decoder's LM, and confirmed the
timestamp-seek parse is unaffected since generate() returns only freshly
generated tokens (prefix not echoed).
what_i_learned:
The prompt channel splits cleanly into two distinct uses with opposite risk
profiles: a running-transcript prefix (iter_011) couples each window to the
model's own prior errors and amplifies them (cer 0.27), whereas a fixed
correctly-spelled glossary prefix has no error-propagation path — its bias is
constant and correct by construction. This makes the channel usable as a pure
lexical prior on domain terms, the one error axis (substitution of domain
vocabulary) that no acoustic re-search knob (greedy/temperature/beam) can
reach.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (57%, length_ratio 0.94 healthy) = wrong-character
domain-term spellings, not coverage. Priming each window's decode with a
static glossary of high-frequency insurance/call-center terms steers the LM
toward correct spellings of exactly those terms, lowering substitution CER
without the iter_011 amplification risk. Decode kept single greedy so the
glossary prefix is the only variable.

capability_investigated:
The spectral character of the waveform input to transcribe() before
processor()/log-mel extraction — distinct from iter_009's amplitude/loudness
probe. Specifically whether Whisper's frozen front end applies pre-emphasis
(a high-frequency shelf) or feeds the raw waveform to the mel filterbank.
what_i_learned:
Whisper's feature extractor applies NO pre-emphasis — it is a plain log-mel
front end, unlike a classic MFCC pipeline. So the high-frequency consonant
band that 8 kHz telephony attenuates (the 0715 batch is band-limited
call-center audio) reaches the mel filterbank already rolled off, with no
front-end compensation. This spectral tilt is a numpy-only, input-side lever
(y[n]=x[n]-0.97·x[n-1]) that the pipeline has never conditioned on; loudness
rescaling (iter_009) cannot reach it because it is amplitude-flat, not
spectrally shaped.
hypothesis:
Apply a first-order pre-emphasis filter to the full waveform before windowing
to lift the consonant-cue upper band telephony attenuates, raising mel
contrast in exactly the bands that disambiguate confusable Korean domain
characters — the dominant substitution axis (sub 57%, length_ratio 0.94
healthy). Decode reverts to a single greedy pass + timestamp seek (ladder
dropped) to isolate the spectral lever as the only variable.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam_size + patience search channel (ledger iter_010) wired as
the DETERMINISTIC first pass of the parent's temperature-fallback ladder
(family_005 / iter_008), rather than as a standalone K-best decode. Studied
whether beam search composes with the existing return_scores gate while
keeping num_hypotheses at the default 1 so res.sequences_ids[0]/res.scores[0]
parsing stays byte-identical to the parent.
what_i_learned:
The parent's gate accepts the FIRST temperature that clears both thresholds,
so a confident-but-wrong greedy commit (high logprob, the signature of the
substitution-dominant axis) passes at t=0.0 and the temperature ladder never
fires for it — the ladder only rescues low-logprob or repetition-collapse
windows. Replacing only the t=0.0 pass with beam_size=5 makes that
first-and-usually-final decode select by global cumulative log-prob instead
of local greedy argmax, which is the one lever that searches AROUND a bad
local commit; sampling fallbacks must stay beam_size=1 (beam>1 + sampling is
contradictory). Keeping num_hypotheses=1 avoids iter_010's K-best parse path.
hypothesis:
Beam search on the deterministic pass lowers substitution (57%, length_ratio
0.94 healthy) by replacing greedy commits with globally-scored hypotheses on
exactly the clean windows the temperature gate currently waves through, while
the unchanged fallback ladder still handles low-confidence/repetition windows.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses K-best return list (res.sequences_ids as a
score-ranked list of K hypotheses, res.scores their log-probs) — the channel
iter_010 confirmed exists but which no pipeline has ever consumed past index
[0]. Studied whether the K beam hypotheses can be combined rather than
ranked, i.e. used as a vote instead of a sorted list.
what_i_learned:
A beam search's K-best list is not K independent transcripts — the
hypotheses share an identical prefix/suffix on confident spans and diverge
only at the low-margin decision points, which on this substitution-dominant
batch are the domain-term forks. That makes the K-best list an implicit
per-fork vote, so it is consumable by an agreement criterion (minimum-Bayes-
risk: smallest summed normalized char edit distance to the rest of the set),
not just by the score ranking every prior iteration used. Selection by
agreement reaches confident-but-wrong forks that score-argmax cannot, because
there the wrong path is the higher-scoring one.
hypothesis:
Replace top-hypothesis selection with MBR consensus over a single
beam_size=5/num_hypotheses=5 decode: pick the hypothesis minimizing expected
edit distance to the K-best set, so an outlier substitution present in only
one or two beams is voted down to the majority spelling. Decode cost equals a
plain beam_size=5 search, keeping runtime at the champion's level.

capability_investigated:
The timestamp channel (iter_004) used not as a seek pointer but as an
absolute-time dedup key across deliberately OVERLAPPING input windows —
i.e. whether successive 30s windows can share acoustic context by starting
before the prior emission ended, while still producing a non-overlapping
transcript. Studied how each segment's relative timestamp token composes with
the window's own start offset (window_start + start_rel) into a global clock.
what_i_learned:
Every long-form pipeline so far advanced seek to exactly where speech ended,
so each window's first segment is decoded with zero left acoustic run-up —
the cold edge where a context-starved decode commits a confident-but-wrong
domain-term spelling, which matches the substitution-dominant / coverage-
healthy profile. The timestamp tokens are per-window-relative but compose into
an absolute clock once offset by the window start, so overlapping windows can
re-decode a region for left-context and be deduplicated by abs_start >=
emitted_until — making acoustic warm-up reachable without double-emitting and
without any backend channel beyond the timestamps already in hand.
hypothesis:
Start each window _OVERLAP_SECONDS (5s) before the last committed boundary so
the formerly-cold left edge is re-decoded with real run-up audio, and gate
emission on absolute segment start so the overlap is discarded. If edge-of-
window substitutions drive the dominant axis, giving those segments left
context should lower sub-rate without touching coverage. Single beam decode
per window; temperature ladder dropped to isolate the segmentation effect.

capability_investigated:
The waveform input before processor()/log-mel extraction, specifically the
INTRA-file dynamic range — distinct from iter_009 (global flat loudness) and
iter_013 (spectral tilt). I reasoned about how Whisper's per-input-max mel
normalisation (log_spec - log_spec.max()) interacts with within-window level
variation rather than with the spectrum or a uniform scale.
what_i_learned:
A flat per-file (or per-window) gain is provably invariant under Whisper's
per-input-max normalisation (iter_009's lesson, generalised: any uniform
scalar multiplies the linear spectrogram and is removed by the max
subtraction). The ONLY amplitude transform that survives that normalisation
is a non-linear one that changes the loud/quiet RATIO within a window — i.e.
dynamic-range compression. The diagnosis shows that ratio is large (rms_db
p05->p95 spans 40-70 dB per file), so a loud burst inside a 30s window crushes
surrounding quiet speech toward the -8 mel floor, yielding low-contrast
features consistent with the confident-but-wrong / coverage-healthy profile.
hypothesis:
Replace the basin pipeline with a clean beam+timestamp-seek decode preceded by
an envelope compander: derive a short-time RMS gain curve that boosts quiet
frames toward the speech median and attenuates loud bursts (beta=0.6, gain
clamped 0.3-8x), with silence frames pinned to unity gain so noise is never
amplified into hallucination. This shrinks intra-window dynamic range, which
survives mel normalisation and should sharpen features on the buried-quiet
spans that drive substitutions.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_no_speech_prob kwarg and the res.no_speech_prob field —
the encoder's <|nospeech|> posterior. iter_006 confirmed this channel exists
but every subsequent pipeline read only sequences_ids and scores; no pipeline
ever requested or branched on no_speech_prob.
what_i_learned:
no_speech_prob is acoustically ORTHOGONAL to the decode's avg_logprob: a beam
search maximises cumulative log-prob and so makes even a hallucinated path on
near-silence MORE confident, meaning a logprob/compression gate (the
champion's) provably cannot separate confident-real from confident-
hallucinated — they are identical on the score channel. The <|nospeech|>
posterior is the only frozen-surface signal that distinguishes them, and
Whisper's reference rule (no_speech_prob>0.6 AND avg_logprob<-1.0 => drop)
pairs the two channels so genuine low-confidence speech is not suppressed.
hypothesis:
Replace the entire 6-temperature fallback ladder with a single deterministic
beam pass per window plus the no_speech_prob non-speech gate. The champion's
hallucination regressed to 0.18 (two files flagged) because beam search
confidently decodes silence windows; gating those out should cut the
hallucinated substitutions/insertions they inject while leaving real-speech
coverage (seek still advances) and the beam global-logprob search intact.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam search width vs. patience as distinct levers on the
deterministic t=0.0 first pass (parent family_005/iter_014). Studied which
of the two actually controls whether a locally-lower-ranked but correct
domain-term path survives to the final hypothesis set.
what_i_learned:
Beam WIDTH and patience act on different stages of the search: patience only
relaxes the stopping criterion (waits for more completed hypotheses), but a
path that drops below the live beam_size at any single step is pruned
immediately regardless of patience. So for the substitution axis — a correct
domain-term spelling that is momentarily lower-ranked at a low-margin fork —
beam width is the binding constraint, not patience.
hypothesis:
Raise the first-pass beam_size 5->8 (patience unchanged) so more low-margin
substitution forks stay alive to global-logprob selection, targeting the
dominant sub 58% axis. Extra compute lands only on the t=0.0 pass that is
almost always accepted; parent runs 225s vs the 719s budget, so 1.6x on that
pass stays well inside budget.

capability_investigated:
Pairing two existing facts in a way the ledger never combined: the input-side
pre-emphasis lever (iter_013, no front-end HF compensation) as a source of
hypothesis DIVERSITY, fed into the num_hypotheses K-best return channel
(iter_010) and the return_scores confidence gate (iter_006). Studied whether
the K-best lists from two different acoustic conditions of the same window can
be pooled into one MBR consensus set.
what_i_learned:
Every rescue in the ledger (temperature ladder iter_008, beam search
iter_010/014/019, within-beam MBR iter_015) draws all its diversity from
re-searching ONE spectrogram, so it structurally cannot escape a
confident-but-wrong spelling that is an artifact of the 8 kHz band-limited
spectrum rather than of the search — the same input reproduces the same
artifact regardless of search width or temperature. Input augmentation
(pre-emphasis restoring the consonant band) is the only lever that perturbs
WHICH spelling is acoustically supported, making a cross-condition vote a
genuinely orthogonal selector to all prior same-input rescues.
hypothesis:
Re-decode each low-confidence (top_score < -1.0 or compression-ratio > 2.4)
window on a pre-emphasized copy, pool its K-best with the original's K-best,
and MBR-select the transcript with minimum summed normalized char edit
distance to the pool. A domain term robust across both conditions appears in
both lists and wins; a spectrum-artifact substitution appears in one and
loses. Confident windows skip the second decode, keeping runtime bounded.

capability_investigated:
The ctranslate2.models.Whisper object that load() returns exposes more than
generate(): its align(features, start_sequence, text_tokens, num_frames)
method, which returns results carrying text_token_probs — a per-token
posterior for a GIVEN token sequence against the audio. No prior iteration
called any method on the model object other than generate().
what_i_learned:
align() makes per-token confidence reachable through the frozen surface (the
model object is returned by load(), so calling .align on it needs no direct
ctranslate2 import). This is granularity that every prior gate lacked:
avg-logprob (iter_006/008/014), no_speech_prob (iter_018) and K-best edit
agreement (iter_015) are all aggregate over the 30s window, so one
low-probability token (the substituted domain term) is diluted by the
surrounding confident tokens. text_token_probs exposes that single weak token
directly.
hypothesis:
Beam-decode each window once (global-log-prob first pass), align the decoded
content tokens against the same features to get per-token probs, and gate on
the WEAKEST token prob, not the average. Only windows with a genuinely
uncertain token (the confident-on-average-but-wrong-on-one-term case that
matches the substitution-dominant / coverage-healthy profile) pay for a
sampled re-decode, and the alternate whose weakest token is strongest is
kept — selecting against the mis-recognized term aggregate scores average away.

capability_investigated:
The object processor(...) returns — inputs.input_features, the final
normalized log-mel array (batch, n_mels, n_frames) the encoder consumes,
exposed as a plain numpy array modifiable before to_storage_view. Every
prior input-side iteration (009 loudness, 013/020 pre-emphasis, 017 dynamic
range) operated on the RAW WAVEFORM before processor(); none touched the
feature array the encoder actually reads.
what_i_learned:
input_features is reachable and mutable through the frozen surface with
numpy alone (processor returns it, to_storage_view takes any np array), so
feature-domain transforms are a distinct lever class from all waveform-domain
probes. A telephone channel's linear distortion is an additive per-mel-bin
offset in log-mel; iter_017 proved a global uniform scalar is invariant under
Whisper's max-subtraction, but a per-BIN offset is non-uniform across bins so
it survives that normalization and genuinely reshapes features — making
per-bin channel mean normalization (CMN) a real, previously-untried transform.
hypothesis:
Subtract each mel bin's temporal mean (removing the channel's constant
per-frequency tilt) and add back the global mean to keep features in
Whisper's expected range, applied per window before generate(). This attacks
the substitution-dominant axis at its acoustic source — the band-limited
channel coloration that no decode-search knob (beam/temp/MBR per iter_020)
can escape because it is in the features, not the search.

capability_investigated:
Combining two channels the ledger established separately but never paired:
the beam K-best list (num_hypotheses=K -> res.sequences_ids/res.scores,
iter_010) and model.align(features, start_sequence, [text_tokens],
num_frames).text_token_probs (the per-token acoustic posterior of a GIVEN
sequence, iter_021). I studied whether align's posterior can act as a
re-ranking SELECTOR over the K-best rather than as a single-hypothesis gate.
what_i_learned:
Every selector tried so far (greedy, temperature ladder iter_008, beam
iter_010/014, K-best MBR iter_015) ranks by the decoder's cumulative
log-prob, which folds in the LM prior — so on a fluent-but-wrong domain-term
spelling the score channel is biased toward the exact substitution we need to
escape, and harder search of that same channel cannot fix it. align()'s
text_token_probs is an acoustic-conditioned posterior orthogonal to that LM
bias, so it is a structurally different ranking key over the same K
hypotheses; unlike iter_021 it scores whole COMPETING hypotheses, not one
hypothesis's weak token in isolation.
hypothesis:
Decode each window with beam_size=5/num_hypotheses=5; when the top-two beams'
avg log-probs are within 0.10 (a low-margin fork, where iter_015 showed the
hypotheses diverge on domain terms), re-rank those two by mean
align().text_token_probs and keep the more acoustically-supported spelling.
Confident windows commit to the top beam with no align call, bounding the
extra teacher-forced passes to ambiguous windows only.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prev-text prompt channel (iter_005) combined with the
return_scores confidence channel (iter_006), used to build a language prior
ONLINE from the model's own output across a long call, rather than from a
raw running tail (iter_011) or a fixed external list (iter_012).
what_i_learned:
The 0715 calls run 600-2600s with 31-383 speech segments on one insurance
topic, so domain vocab recurs many times within a single recording. That
makes the model's own confident, RECURRING content tokens a correct-by-
recurrence prior with no error-propagation path: filtering harvested tokens
by an avg-logprob gate, a recurrence>=2 count, and >=2 stripped chars
(dropping one-off mis-decodes and bare particles) yields a self-glossary
distinct from both iter_011 (error-coupled raw tail, cer 0.27) and iter_012
(hand-curated static list). generate() returns only freshly generated tokens
under a prev-text prefix, so the timestamp-seek parse is unaffected.
hypothesis:
Feeding the harvested-so-far recurring-term glossary through <|startofprev|>
ahead of SOT on each window biases the decoder toward the spellings it
already committed to confidently elsewhere in the call, recovering domain
terms that a later quiet/noisy window's band-limited audio cannot support on
its own — the window-local substitutions no acoustic re-search can reach.

capability_investigated:
The additive-noise statistics of the raw waveform before processor()/log-mel
extraction — the per-frequency-bin background noise floor, estimated via a
numpy STFT (np.fft.rfft over Hann frames). Distinct from every prior input
probe: iter_009 (loudness, invariant under per-input-max mel norm), iter_013/020
(pre-emphasis HF tilt), iter_017 (dynamic range), iter_022 (feature-domain CMN).
what_i_learned:
The stationary noise floor of band-limited call-center audio is recoverable
with numpy alone and modifiable before processor(): because speech is
intermittent, the low percentile of each STFT bin across frames is a robust
per-bin noise estimate (minimum statistics), and Hann 50% overlap satisfies
COLA so magnitude spectral subtraction reconstructs cleanly via overlap-add
with preserved phase. This is an input transform NOT invariant under Whisper's
per-input-max mel normalization (it is non-uniform across both time and
frequency, unlike a flat scalar) and it is acoustically orthogonal to every
decode-side rescue, which all re-search the same corrupted spectrogram.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (58%, coverage healthy) because noise masks the weak
consonant energy that disambiguates domain-term spellings on 8 kHz telephony;
no beam/temperature/MBR/align rescue can escape an artifact of the noise bed
rather than the search. Attenuating that bed before feature extraction changes
which spelling is acoustically supported. Decode simplified to one beam pass so
the denoiser is the lever; preprocessing is CPU-only so the budget is safe.

capability_investigated:
The timestamp channel (iter_004) + absolute-clock composition (iter_016) used
not as a seek pointer within one pass but as the join key between TWO
independent full long-form decodes run at different window phase offsets
(0s and ~15s start). Studied whether segment left-context (seconds decoded
before a segment inside its own window, derivable from start_rel alone) is a
reconciliation key that needs no extra return channel.
what_i_learned:
Every rescue in the ledger (temperature ladder iter_008, beam iter_010/014,
K-best MBR iter_015, align-rerank iter_023, input-condition vote iter_020)
keeps ONE segmentation fixed and only varies search hardness or input
condition over that single covering — so a domain term landing on a window
seam is cut identically on every search and stays substituted. Window phase
is a previously-unused axis: shifting the seek origin by ~15s relocates every
seam, so a cold context-starved segment in one pass (lc≈0) is a fully
left-contexted interior segment in the other. The decoder's own start_rel
timestamp gives per-segment left-context for free, making an interiority-based
cross-pass reconciliation buildable through the frozen surface with no channel
beyond the timestamps already in hand.
hypothesis:
Decode the recording twice via the standard timestamp-seek loop at phase
offsets 0s and 15s, parse each window into absolute-clock segments tagged with
left-context, then reconcile: where both passes cover the same time region
(start within 1.5s) keep the segment with greater left-context. This attacks
the cold-edge substitution axis directly while two beam=2 passes cost less
than the champion's beam=5 + temperature-fallback single pass.

capability_investigated:
model.align(features, start_seq, [content_tokens], num_frames).text_token_probs
(ledger iter_021/023) used not as a K-best re-ranker but as a per-segment
LOCALIZER: averaging the acoustic posterior over each timestamp-delimited
segment to flag acoustically thin segments, paired with re-decoding those
segments' audio cropped in ISOLATION so Whisper's per-input-max mel
normalization (iter_009/017) re-normalizes the crop to its own loudest frame.
what_i_learned:
align()'s text_token_probs is per-token and assignable to timestamp segments
by decode order, giving a segment-granularity acoustic-confidence map the
aggregate window score (iter_006/018) cannot resolve; and because the front
end normalizes per-input, cropping a segment to its own extent is a distinct
INPUT condition from that segment embedded mid-30s-window — the only ledger
rescues left untried localize the costly beam re-decode to where the acoustic
posterior is weak instead of re-searching the whole fixed spectrogram.
hypothesis:
A cheap greedy survey pass gives timestamp segmentation; align localizes the
acoustically weakest segments; the bounded beam isolation re-decode (capped,
threshold-gated) replaces only those, targeting confident-but-wrong
substitutions that LM-biased re-search of the same window cannot escape.

capability_investigated:
The num_hypotheses K-best return list (res.sequences_ids/res.scores, iter_010/015)
and the sampled-path channel (iter_008) consumed together as POSITIONAL voters
rather than as whole-sequence candidates to rank/select. Studied whether the
per-hypothesis emit-region texts can be character-aligned (difflib SequenceMatcher,
pure CPU) to a skeleton and fused position-by-position through the frozen surface.
what_i_learned:
Every selector the ledger built (greedy, temperature ladder iter_008, beam
iter_010/014, MBR iter_015, align-rerank iter_023) commits to ONE whole hypothesis
chosen by a score channel that is LM-biased toward the exact fluent substitution to
escape, so the wrong spelling is the higher-scoring one and no ranking of whole
sequences can leave it. The K-best hypotheses agree on confident spans and diverge
only at the low-margin domain-term forks, so a per-character weighted-majority vote
(weight=exp(avg_logprob)) over the K-best plus one off-beam sample is well-defined and
can override the top path at a single fork — a flip whole-hypothesis selection cannot
make. Both channels (K-best emit texts, sampled emit text) are reachable per window
with two generate() calls; seek stays on the top beam hypothesis's timestamps so
coverage is untouched.
hypothesis:
Replace whole-hypothesis selection with confidence-weighted positional ROVER fusion:
decode each window with beam_size=5/num_hypotheses=3 (fork voters) plus one
full-distribution sampled decode (off-beam voter), align each voter's emit-region text
to the highest-weight skeleton, and emit the per-position weighted majority. Targets
the substitution-dominant axis (sub 58%, length_ratio 0.95 healthy) by letting agreeing
lower-ranked voters correct a confident-but-wrong top-path domain term.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s suppress_tokens decode kwarg (ctranslate2 Whisper.generate
accepts suppress_blank / suppress_tokens, where -1 selects the default
special-token suppression and explicit ids hard-ban those tokens at every
decode step). No prior iteration ever passed suppress_tokens — every pipeline
let the beam emit from the full vocabulary. Paired with align()'s
text_token_probs (iter_021/027) to pick which ids to ban.
what_i_learned:
suppress_tokens is a structurally different lever from every selector in the
ledger: temperature ladder, beam, K-best MBR, align-rerank and positional
vote all re-RANK the decoder's own candidate set, whose score channel is
LM-biased toward the fluent-but-wrong spelling, so the wrong path keeps
winning. A hard ban DELETES that token from the search, so the beam is forced
onto the next-best acoustic path the ranking could never reach. The ban list
is well-defined: align()'s acoustic posterior (LM-free) flags content tokens
that score high in the beam but fit the audio poorly — the substitution
suspects — and accepting the re-decode only when its mean align posterior
beats the original keeps the selection on the acoustic axis, not the score.
hypothesis:
Per window, beam-decode, align the content tokens, ban the small set
(1.._MAX_SUPPRESS) whose acoustic posterior < 0.25, and re-decode with
suppress_tokens=[-1, *weak]; keep the forced path only if its content's mean
align posterior is higher. Removing the confident-but-wrong domain-term token
from the search directly attacks the dominant substitution axis (sub 58%,
length_ratio healthy) in a way no re-ranking of the same paths can.

capability_investigated:
The ctranslate2.models.Whisper object returned by load() — specifically its
detect_language(features) method, the third model-object method besides
generate() and align(), which runs the encoder alone and returns a per-batch
list of (language_token, probability) pairs. No prior iteration ever called
it; the ledger's confidence gates all read decoder-side channels (scores
iter_006, no_speech_prob iter_018) or align()'s per-token posterior (iter_021).
what_i_learned:
detect_language exposes the ENCODER's language posterior through the frozen
surface with no extra import (it is a method on the load() object, like align
in iter_021). This is an acoustic-confidence signal structurally distinct from
every gate the ledger built: avg_logprob is decoder-cumulative and LM-biased
toward the fluent substitution to escape, so it stays HIGH on confident-wrong
domain terms; no_speech_prob only separates speech from silence. The encoder
language posterior instead drops when the 8 kHz band degrades a window enough
that the encoder cannot cleanly resolve it — a free, pre-decode triage signal
for exactly the substitution-risky windows, readable before any decoded token.
hypothesis:
Gate on the encoder Korean posterior: confident windows (p_ko>=0.85) decode
once via beam and commit; a window below threshold is acoustically ambiguous
(band-degraded, substitution-risky), so re-decode it from a pre-emphasized
waveform (restores the consonant band Whisper's front end leaves rolled off,
iter_013) and keep the higher-avg-logprob decode. The two decodes are
different INPUT conditions, not two searches of one spectrogram, so the
re-decode can support a different domain-term spelling. The gate keeps the
second encode+decode off clean windows, holding runtime near one beam pass
plus a cheap encoder forward per window.

capability_investigated:
processor(...).input_features as an EQUALIZATION surface (not a normalization
one): the normalized log-mel array fed verbatim to the encoder via
to_storage_view (mutable, ledger iter_022), modified by a deterministic
per-mel-bin additive gain ramp over the upper bins.
what_i_learned:
A per-mel-bin additive gain ramp is a distinct input lever from every prior
input probe: it is not invariant under Whisper's per-input-max normalization
(it is non-uniform across bins, like iter_022's CMN) but unlike CMN it does
not re-center — it imposes a fixed monotone tilt on the mel axis the encoder
reads. Because input_features is consumed directly (iter_022), the EQ is the
final feature seen, so a waveform pre-emphasis shelf (iter_013/020, which
passes through the whole front end) and a direct mel-axis ramp are separable
levers. This targets the 8 kHz consonant-band rolloff that drives consonant
substitution, an axis no decode-side re-search can reach.
hypothesis:
Lift the upper ~45% of mel bins by a linear additive ramp (peak +0.30 in
log-mel units, features ~[-1,1]) on each window's input_features before the
encoder, restoring consonant-band contrast so confident-but-wrong domain-term
spellings flip to the correct acoustically-supported path. Decode is a single
beam pass with timestamp seek (ladder/gate removed) to measure the EQ alone.

capability_investigated:
The timestamp channel (iter_004) composed into an absolute clock (iter_016),
used to parse each window into timestamp-delimited segments and decide
per-segment commit/defer — rather than as a single seek pointer to the last
timestamp. Studied whether a window's RIGHT-EDGE segment (decoded with no
in-window right-context) can be deferred and re-decoded as an interior,
fully bilaterally-contexted segment of the next overlapping window.
what_i_learned:
Every windowing pipeline in the ledger (blind 30s, energy VAD, champion's
timestamp-seek-to-last) structurally COMMITS each window's final segment —
the one segment Whisper decodes with zero right run-up, exactly where a
context-starved decoder locks a confident-but-wrong domain-term spelling.
The timestamp tokens expose enough per-segment boundaries on an absolute
clock (window_start + rel) to commit only interior segments and re-seek to
just before the last committed boundary, so the deferred edge segment
reappears as an interior segment downstream. abs_start is a sound dedup key
(skip start < committed_until), making overlap re-decode without double-emit
buildable from the timestamps already in hand — no extra return channel. This
perturbs WHICH features the edge segment is decoded against (right-context
amount), structurally distinct from all decode-side re-search that re-ranks
the same fixed context-starved features.
hypothesis:
Deferring and re-decoding each window's least-right-contexted segment as a
downstream interior segment gives the substitution-prone edge tokens full
bilateral acoustic context, attacking the dominant substitution axis at its
structural source (cold edge commits) rather than by re-ranking the same
features. Content-driven re-seek (not fixed stride) guards coverage against
early-stopping windows.

capability_investigated:
model.align(features, start_seq, [content_tokens], num_frames).text_token_probs
(ledger iter_021/023/027) used as a selector ACROSS two acoustic input
conditions — raw normalized log-mel vs per-mel-bin channel-mean-normalized
(CMN, iter_022) — with both candidates scored against the SAME raw features.
what_i_learned:
align()'s posterior and the cross-condition diversity axis (iter_020) are
separable from the two ways the ledger already used them: iter_020 pooled
cross-condition candidates by TEXT agreement (MBR over hypotheses), and
iter_023 reranked SAME-condition K-best by align. Scoring two DIFFERENT-input
candidates against the one canonical raw spectrogram is a third, untried
composition — the diversity perturbs which spelling is acoustically supported
(breaking the band-limited artifact a single-input re-search reproduces) while
the selector stays LM-free on the true audio (escaping the score channel's
bias toward the fluent-but-wrong domain-term spelling). The candidate token
sequences for align are isolable with a single `< eot_id` filter since Whisper
packs eot/specials/timestamps at or above that id.
hypothesis:
Decode each window on raw features (beam); on windows whose raw avg-logprob is
below a clean gate (substitution risk concentrates there, and the gate bounds
the extra compute), also decode a CMN variant, then commit to whichever
candidate scores higher under align() on the raw features. This should flip
confident-but-wrong consonant/domain-term forks that all same-input re-search
in the ledger leaves substituted, without touching coverage (seek unchanged).

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prev-text prompt channel (ledger iter_005) decoupled from
decode across two passes — studied whether the recurrence-gated self-glossary
(iter_024) can be harvested from a COMPLETE cheap pass-1 survey and then
applied globally to pass-2, rather than built forward/incrementally inside a
single pass.
what_i_learned:
iter_024's incremental harvest has a structural blind spot the ledger never
named: the glossary is empty/sparse for the early windows of a call, yet that
is exactly where domain vocabulary first appears (greeting, product/plan
names) with zero prior context — the cold-start substitutions. A two-pass
split makes the prior bidirectional: a term recurring late in the call is in
the glossary when window 0 decodes. Because generate() returns only freshly
generated tokens under a prev prefix (iter_005/012/024), the global glossary
prefix leaves the timestamp-seek parse byte-identical; the only cost is one
extra greedy survey pass, which is cheaper than the beam pass it precedes.
hypothesis:
A cheap greedy pass-1 harvests content token ids recurring >=2x across the
whole call (from confident windows only, >=2 stripped chars), capped to 180
tokens; pass-2 prefixes EVERY window with [<|startofprev|>]+glossary+SOT and
beam-decodes. Giving the cold call opening the same lexical prior as the rest
should cut the cold-start domain-term substitutions the forward-only iter_024
could not reach.

capability_investigated:
processor(...).input_features as a TIME-axis surface — the post-normalization
(batch, n_mels, n_frames) log-mel array the encoder reads verbatim via
to_storage_view (mutable, iter_022), modified along the FRAME axis rather than
the mel-bin axis every prior feature probe used (iter_022 CMN, iter_031 ramp).
what_i_learned:
Each frame's mean over mel bins is a free per-frame loudness readout on the
already-normalized features, so a per-frame additive lift is a distinct lever
class from all prior input probes: unlike a waveform DRC (which passes through
Whisper's per-input-max subtraction and is partly re-flattened by it), an
offset added directly to input_features lands AFTER that subtraction and is
not undone — making time-axis dynamic-range compression a real, untried
transform separable from both frequency-axis feature edits and every
waveform-domain amplitude probe.
hypothesis:
iter_017's diagnosis is that a loud burst inside a 30s window sets the max
reference and crushes neighbouring quiet domain-term speech toward the mel
floor (low-contrast features → confident-wrong substitutions). Lifting frames
below the window's p75 level toward it (capped, silence-floor frames excluded
to avoid hallucination) compresses the loud/quiet ratio along time so quiet
speech regains contrast before the encoder sees it — attacking the dominant
substitution axis on a feature axis no decode re-search or prior input probe
reaches.

capability_investigated:
processor(...).input_features as a SPECTRAL-SHAPE surface — the normalized
log-mel array (1, n_mels, n_frames) fed to the encoder verbatim via
to_storage_view (mutable, iter_022). Studied the within-frame mel-axis
envelope SHAPE (relative bin-to-bin contrast), distinct from the level/offset
transforms every prior feature probe applied along that same axis.
what_i_learned:
Every input-feature edit in the ledger is a level shift that leaves spectral
CONTRAST unchanged: iter_031's per-bin additive ramp is a monotone tilt,
iter_035's per-frame lift is a constant time-axis offset, iter_022's CMN only
re-centers per bin — all are additive and commute with smoothing, so none
touches the height of a formant peak relative to its neighbours. The only
mel-axis operation that changes envelope contrast is a NON-additive one: a
high-pass / unsharp mask (F + alpha*(F - boxsmooth_mel(F))) amplifies peaks
and valleys relative to the slowly-varying mean, and because it lands after
Whisper's per-input-max subtraction it is not undone — a genuinely untried
feature transform that is invariant on flat/tilted envelopes (the prior
probes) but active on formant/consonant structure.
hypothesis:
The substitution profile (sub 58%, length_ratio 0.95 healthy) is wrong-
character domain terms on 8 kHz band-limited audio whose consonant band
reaches the filterbank rolled off and smeared (iter_013, no pre-emphasis),
giving a low-contrast envelope where adjacent phonemes look alike. A mel-axis
unsharp mask (kernel 7 bins, alpha 0.6) restores that spectral contrast
before the encoder sees it, perturbing WHICH spelling is acoustically
supported — orthogonal to all decode-side re-search (same smeared features)
and to all level-shift input probes. Single beam pass isolates the lever.

capability_investigated:
The decoded TEXT itself as a corpus surface — not the input features and not
any generate()/align() return channel, but the cross-window redundancy in the
final transcript string. No prior iteration treated the output as a thing with
internal agreement to exploit; every probe touched input or decode.
what_i_learned:
A domain term recurring 30+ times in one 600-2600s call (the recurrence fact
iter_024 used for a prompt glossary) produces a frequent canonical spelling
plus a few rare singleton variants on the windows the search mis-flipped, and
those variants differ by a single INTERIOR Hangul syllable (the 8 kHz
consonant confusion). This majority spelling is a correction signal reachable
with zero extra decode and no backend channel — but it is only safe under a
first+last-syllable equality guard, because Korean inflection (보험을/보험은)
also lives at edit-distance 1 and must be protected at the final particle.
hypothesis:
Run one deterministic beam pass (champion's proven coverage core, ladder
stripped) then snap each singleton word >=4 syllables to an equal-length
canonical anchor (count>=4) sharing its first+last syllable and differing by
<=1 interior syllable. Cross-window agreement corrects the minority of windows
the LM-biased score channel got wrong — orthogonal to all input/decode levers.

capability_investigated:
The batch axis of generate(features, prompts): features carries a leading
(B, n_mels, n_frames) batch dimension and prompts is one token-prompt per
batch entry, returning a list of B WhisperGenerationResults. Every prior
iteration passed a single-window feature array and a single-element prompts
list, so B was always 1 — the batch dimension itself was never used.
what_i_learned:
The same window's feature tensor can be replicated along axis 0 (np.concatenate)
and paired with a list of DIFFERENT decoder prefixes to decode one audio under
N prefix conditions in a SINGLE batched generate() call, rather than N separate
passes. This makes a per-window prefix ensemble (bare SOT vs a fixed-glossary
<|startofprev|> prior) cost one extra beam in the same launch instead of a
second long-form pass (iter_034), and the two results are independently scored
via return_scores for per-window selection — a structurally new use of the
surface, orthogonal to the temperature-ladder / K-best single-prompt decodes.
hypothesis:
Replicate each window's features to batch size 2 and decode cond A (bare SOT)
and cond B (<|startofprev|> + correctly-spelled insurance glossary + SOT) in
one batched beam call, selecting per window by avg log-prob. On a band-limited
domain-term fork (the substitution axis) the glossary prior should pull cond B
toward the correct lexical spelling, while score-based selection prevents it
from forcing a worse path on clear spans.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch-axis multi-prompt path (iter_038) versus issuing the second
prefix condition as a separate single-prompt generate() call — specifically
the backend rule that a BATCHED generate requires <|startoftranscript|> at the
same index in every batch entry, which a <|startofprev|> glossary prefix
shifts.
what_i_learned:
The batch axis cannot carry a bare-SOT prompt and a prev-prefixed prompt
together: ctranslate2's Whisper.generate hard-rejects unequal SOT positions
across batch entries ("requires the <|startoftranscript|> token to be at the
same position in all batches"). So a prefix ensemble must either pad both
prompts to an equal prev-token count or — simpler and constraint-free — run
each condition as its own B=1 generate() call, where SOT position is per-call
and the rule never applies.
hypothesis:
Restore the iter_014 champion and add the glossary-primed condition as a
SEPARATE sequential generate() (not a batch entry), gated to fire only when
cond A's t=0 beam fails the logprob/compression gate — the substitution-risk
windows — then keep whichever of A/B has the higher avg log-prob. This fixes
the exact crash, keeps the champion's beam gains, applies the lexical prior
only where it can help, and adds at most one extra beam pass on uncertain
windows so runtime stays within budget.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses K-best return list (res.sequences_ids ranked,
res.scores their avg log-probs, ledger iter_010/015) consumed as a SELECTION
SURFACE for a lexical feature rather than a score channel — and the fixed
domain glossary used as that feature instead of as a <|startofprev|> prompt
prefix (its only prior use, iter_012/024/034).
what_i_learned:
The glossary and the K-best list were each established separately but never
composed: every glossary use was a prompt prefix (a soft LM bias the decoder
overrides precisely on the substitution forks, since the score channel is
LM-biased toward the fluent-but-wrong spelling), and every K-best consumer
ranked by a score channel (logprob iter_010/014, MBR iter_015, align iter_023)
— never by lexical content. Per iter_015 the K hypotheses diverge only at the
low-margin domain-term forks, so the canonical spelling is typically PRESENT
in the beam at rank>0; a glossary-term count is a near-free selector that can
reach it, and gating promotion to a within-MARGIN logprob band keeps the
choice among only acoustically-plausible paths the model itself produced
(error-propagation-free, unlike a forced prefix).
hypothesis:
Decode each window once with beam_size=5 + num_hypotheses=5 + return_scores,
then within the set of hypotheses whose avg log-prob is within 0.12 of the
best, select the one matching the most canonical glossary terms (tie-break by
log-prob). This lifts the buried canonical-spelling fork the score ranking
loses to the fluent substitution, attacking the dominant substitution axis
(sub 58%) without injecting any text the beam did not already deem plausible.

capability_investigated:
The decoded TEXT decomposed to Hangul jamo (choseong/jungseong/jongseong via
the U+AC00 block arithmetic, pure CPU) as a correction surface against the
fixed domain glossary — distinct from every prior glossary use, which fed it
into the DECODER as a <|startofprev|> soft prompt prior (iter_012/024/034/039)
or a K-best lexical score selector (iter_040), and from iter_037 which voted
cross-window majority at whole-syllable granularity.
what_i_learned:
A glossary used as a soft decoder prior cannot fix a SYSTEMATIC substitution —
one mis-spelled the same consonant-confusion way on every window — because the
score channel is LM-biased toward that fluent-wrong spelling and a cross-window
majority (iter_037) only has the wrong spelling to vote on. Jamo decomposition
makes the choseong/jungseong/jongseong of each output syllable separable, so a
"consonant-only, same-vowel, single interior syllable" diff to a curated
correct lexicon is expressible and isolates exactly the 8 kHz band-limit
confusion while leaving onset-distinct words and Korean inflection (보험을/보험은,
protected by particle-strip + vowel-identity guards) untouched. The correction
is error-propagation-free because the target spelling is fixed and correct.
hypothesis:
Hard-correcting each decoded word to its unambiguous consonant-only glossary
neighbour (after stripping a trailing particle, requiring identical first
syllable and identical vowels) repairs the systematic domain-term substitution
the decoder commits identically on every window — the dominant axis (sub 58%,
length_ratio 0.95 healthy) — which no decode-side re-search or cross-window
majority can reach; decode keeps the robust gate so coverage is unchanged.

capability_investigated:
processor(...).input_features (mutable, fed to encoder verbatim via
to_storage_view, iter_022) treated as a FREQUENCY-WARP surface: resampling
the mel-bin axis by a factor alpha (vocal-tract-length perturbation) so
formant energy MOVES between bins, rather than the additive level/contrast
edits every prior feature probe applied along that same axis.
what_i_learned:
A mel-bin-axis warp is a distinct lever class from all prior cross-condition
diversity: pre-emphasis (iter_020), CMN (iter_033) and the feature edits
(iter_031 ramp, iter_035 lift, iter_036 unsharp) are all additive/scaling ops
that re-weight bins in place and leave each formant peak on the SAME bin, so a
band-limit substitution tied to peak POSITION survives all of them; only a
warp (interp of the bin axis by m/alpha) relocates the peak, making two warps
independent acoustic witnesses of a domain-term fork. Decoding two warped
copies with cheap greedy and overwriting a canonical-emit span only where both
warps yield the IDENTICAL difflib 'replace' is a coverage-preserving,
LM-free-agreement substitution fix reachable with numpy + generate() alone.
hypothesis:
The substitution axis (sub 58%, coverage healthy) is dominated by
confident-but-wrong domain-term spellings the score channel keeps winning;
two formant-warp geometries that independently agree on a different spelling
vote down that artifact where no in-place level/contrast condition could.

capability_investigated:
The waveform short-time RMS energy envelope (the channel iter_009/017/025
used only for amplitude normalization) repurposed as a BOUNDARY-PLACEMENT
signal — choosing where each decode window starts/ends — rather than as a
feature-scaling input. Also confirmed the processor's padding contract:
processor() zero-pads any <=30s chunk to the fixed 30s log-mel the encoder
needs, so a variable-length silence-bounded segment is a valid generate()
input with no special handling.
what_i_learned:
Window-boundary position is a free, coverage-SAFE lever the ledger never
touched: because every sample falls into exactly one segment, the silence
threshold only RELOCATES boundaries and can never delete speech, so unlike a
silence-removing VAD this is incapable of regressing length_ratio. All prior
windowing (blind 30s, champion seek-to-last-timestamp, overlap iter_016/026/032)
cuts on a fixed clock, so a seam lands mid-word identically on every pass; and
the processor padding fact means <=30s silence-bounded segments need no
in-window timestamp seek at all.
hypothesis:
Placing boundaries at silence-gap midpoints (numpy RMS, p95-relative -35dB,
>=0.5s gaps, 28s cap with hard-cut fallback for >28s speech runs) prevents
domain terms being split across a fixed 30s seam — a structural source of the
confident-but-wrong substitution — and prevents pure-silence 30s windows (the
hallucination_hit flag on the two high-silence focus files), with no overlap
/reconciliation cost and no coverage loss by construction.

capability_investigated:
model.align(features, start_sequence, text_tokens, num_frames).text_token_probs
(iter_021) batched over TWO content-token sequences in one call — the original
decode and an externally-injected lexicon rewrite — to score both against the
same audio. Studied align() as a verifier of a candidate the beam never
emitted, not as a re-ranker/gate over hypotheses the search produced.
what_i_learned:
align() can score a token sequence that did NOT come out of generate() at all:
text_tokens is an arbitrary caller-supplied id list, so a corrected spelling
absent from every beam path is still alignable and gets a per-token acoustic
posterior. Batching [orig_ids, corr_ids] with replicated features and a shared
notimestamps start_sequence yields two posterior vectors comparable token-for-
token; difflib over the two id lists isolates exactly the changed span, so the
gate reads the acoustic evidence for the substituted syllable alone instead of
a window-diluted mean. This is the structural escape from the score channel's
LM bias that every beam-confined selector lacked.
hypothesis:
Rewriting confusion-distance-1 words (same syllable count, identical vowels,
one syllable's consonants changed) toward a curated correct lexicon and
committing only when align's changed-span posterior does not drop will fix
systematic 8 kHz consonant substitutions the beam can never reach, without
iter_041's blind-correction regression — because the audio, not the LM, makes
the final call.

capability_investigated:
model.align(features, start_sequence, [text_tokens], num_frames) returns a
WhisperAlignmentResult whose .alignments field (the per-text-token ->
encoder-frame DTW path) is distinct from .text_token_probs. Every prior
align() use (iter_021/023/027/033/044) read only text_token_probs; the
frame-map channel has never been consumed.
what_i_learned:
.alignments exposes an ACOUSTIC localization of each decoded token in encoder
frames (50 frames/s), reachable on the same already-proven align() call with
no new import. This is a different boundary source than the decoder's own
<|t|> timestamp tokens that every long-form seek has used: the timestamp is an
LM-biased decoded prediction, the alignment frame is where the audio actually
sits — so it can place the window's true right edge and defer the cold edge
token even when the model drops or mis-prints its trailing timestamp.
hypothesis:
Seek by the last content token's alignment frame instead of the last
timestamp token, and defer that final (right-context-starved) token to
re-decode as an interior token in the next overlapping window. Targets the
deletion on long continuous-speech files (01_8088 len 0.91, 01_8098 0.93)
where timestamp-driven seek jumps past un-transcribed audio.

capability_investigated:
The parent (family_006/iter_039) cond-B selection policy: the glossary-primed
<|startofprev|> beam decode is computed on substitution-risk windows but
adopted only when its avg log-prob (res.scores[0], return_scores channel
iter_006) STRICTLY exceeds cond A's. Studied the interaction of that
comparison with the score channel's known LM bias rather than any new channel.
what_i_learned:
cond B fires but is almost never adopted: it only runs when cond A failed the
gate (low-confidence substitution-risk windows), yet the score channel is
LM-biased toward the fluent-but-wrong spelling (ledger iter_040/041), so the
glossary's corrected-domain-term path typically scores SLIGHTLY BELOW the
fluent-wrong cond-A path. A strict ">" therefore rejects exactly the fixes the
glossary was designed to make — the parent paid for cond B's compute without
cashing its benefit. The fix is a policy threshold, not a new mechanism.
hypothesis:
Adopt cond B when its avg log-prob is within a small margin
(_GLOSSARY_LOGPROB_MARGIN=0.1 nats) of cond A's, i.e. res_b.scores[0] >=
lp_a - 0.1, instead of strictly greater. On the substitution-risk windows
(only place cond B runs), trust the fixed-correct domain prior even when it
costs a hair of LM-biased logprob; the tight margin bounds error propagation.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s length_penalty decoding kwarg — listed in the frozen.asr_backend
docstring but never set by any prior iteration. In ctranslate2's beam search
the hypothesis score is the cumulative log-prob normalized by
length ** length_penalty, so this kwarg controls how the beam trades sequence
length against per-token confidence. Studied it as a lever on the DELETION
axis rather than the substitution axis every prior probe attacked.
what_i_learned:
The diagnosis carries an unexploited signal orthogonal to substitution:
length_ratio is < 1.0 on every single file of the 0715 batch (0.91-0.98) and
deletions are 36% of the error mass — a SYSTEMATIC length deficit, not a
per-window accident. Because cumulative log-prob is negative, length_penalty
> 1.0 raises the length normalizer's exponent and lifts longer (more
complete) hypotheses relative to short ones, making it the only decode
channel that acts on the deletion axis directly — every other ledger lever
(glossary, align, K-best, feature edits) re-ranks or biases toward a spelling
and leaves the beam's length normalization untouched.
hypothesis:
Stripping the pipeline back to a single deterministic beam pass with
length_penalty=2.0 (vs the default ~1.0) should reduce the systematic
short-clipping that drives the 36% deletion mass, raising length_ratio toward
1.0 and lowering corpus_cer through coverage rather than the stalled
substitution route. Removed the glossary/temperature-ladder/cond-B machinery
so the coverage lever is measured in isolation, not as a knob on the
substitution champion.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_no_speech_prob kwarg and res.no_speech_prob — the
encoder's <|nospeech|> posterior (ledger iter_018) — composed with the two
grafted parents (family_005 beam first pass, family_006 glossary cond-B
margin), which both maximise a confident decode path.
what_i_learned:
no_speech_prob is encoder-side, so it is identical across every decode of a
window's features and can be read once off cond A's beam pass with no extra
encoder run. It is acoustically orthogonal to avg_logprob: beam search and the
glossary LM prior both make a hallucinated near-silence path MORE confident, so
the logprob/compression gate cannot separate confident-real from confident-
hallucinated — only the <|nospeech|> posterior can. Whisper's paired rule
(no_speech>0.6 AND avg_logprob<-1.0) fires only on windows that failed every
gate, so gate-passing and genuine low-confidence speech survive.
hypothesis:
Both parents are already in the champion and both lift substitution by
maximising a confident path; neither guards the hallucination that confidence-
maximisation induces on near-silent windows (both focus files flagged
hallucination_hit/guard_violation). Adding the no_speech_prob paired gate drops
exactly those spurious-text windows, cutting hallucination-driven insertion/
substitution while the deletion-safe AND condition protects real speech.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s sampling_topp (nucleus) decode kwarg — listed under the
docstring's "sampling_*" but never set by any ledger iteration. Every prior
sampled decode (temperature ladder iter_008, off-beam voter iter_028) used
sampling_topk=0 (full untruncated distribution) under a temperature; topp
truncates each step to the smallest token set covering mass p BEFORE
sampling, a structurally different diversity source.
what_i_learned:
Nucleus truncation requires lifting ctranslate2's default sampling_topk=1
cap (set sampling_topk=0) for topp to have any effect; otherwise the top-1
argmax makes the draw deterministic and topp is inert. Unlike full-tail
sampling, nucleus draws stay inside the model's plausible alternatives, so
independent samples can CONCENTRATE on a coherent alternative spelling at a
low-margin fork — making cross-sample agreement a usable, LM-free selector
that a full-tail voter (which sees one-off rare-tail garbage) cannot form.
hypothesis:
Beam pass owns text + seek (coverage untouched, immune to the iter_045
re-segmentation blow-up); on gate-failing substitution-risk windows, draw 3
nucleus samples and overwrite a span only where >=2 samples independently
propose the IDENTICAL equal-length replacement against the beam text. Equal
length keeps it coverage-neutral, attacking sub 58% without touching del/ins
or Korean inflection at span edges.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s sampling_topp kwarg and the ctranslate2 Whisper.generate
signature as fully enumerated by iter_049's TypeError dump.
what_i_learned:
sampling_topp is NOT an accepted argument of ctranslate2's Whisper.generate
in this build — the crash's own error printout lists the COMPLETE supported
kwarg set (beam_size, patience, num_hypotheses, length_penalty,
repetition_penalty, no_repeat_ngram_size, max_length, return_scores,
return_logits_vocab, return_no_speech_prob, max_initial_timestamp_index,
suppress_blank, suppress_tokens, sampling_topk, sampling_temperature) and
there is no topp/nucleus knob. Nucleus sampling is therefore unreachable
through the frozen surface; the only sampled-diversity lever is
sampling_topk + sampling_temperature (full-tail).
hypothesis:
Since the nucleus path is impossible, restore the champion (iter_046) and
make the minimal failure-targeted edit: trim the fallback ladder from
(0.0..1.0) to (0.0,0.2,0.4,0.6). The high-temp rungs are full-tail (the noisy
diversity source the ledger flagged), essentially never clear a gate that
0.4/0.6 don't, and only risk committing high-temp garbage via the
best_logprob fallback — so trimming them is coverage-neutral, keeps the
repetition-escape, cuts runtime, and is guaranteed to run.

capability_investigated:
The parent's (family_006/iter_046) cond-B trigger condition — the predicate
that decides on WHICH windows the glossary-primed <|startofprev|> beam runs.
It currently reuses the acceptance gate's _LOGPROB_THRESHOLD (-1.0), so the
cond-B firing set is identical to the gate-failure set. Studied the trigger's
coverage against the score channel's known LM bias, not any new channel.
what_i_learned:
cond B's firing set is mis-targeted: it only runs when cond A fully fails the
gate (lp_a < -1.0), but the dominant failure is the confident-but-WRONG
domain term — the score channel is LM-biased toward the fluent substitution
(ledger iter_040/041), so a substituted window still scores well above -1.0,
PASSES the gate, and cond B never runs on it at all. The trigger threshold is
therefore a distinct lever from the adoption margin (iter_046 tuned the
margin; the windows that reach that comparison are set by the trigger).
hypothesis:
Decouple the cond-B trigger from the acceptance gate and raise it to -0.5,
so the glossary prior also fires on the borderline-confident band
[-1.0, -0.5] — the confident-wrong substitution windows the gate lets pass.
Acceptance stays at -1.0 and adoption stays margin-gated, so coverage and
error-propagation bounds are unchanged; only cond B's reach toward the
dominant substitution axis widens. Runtime headroom (229s vs 719s) absorbs
the extra beam passes on the band.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_logits_vocab decode kwarg and the res.logits channel it
populates — the FULL per-step vocabulary logit distribution along the emitted
path. Confirmed an accepted arg by iter_050's TypeError dump but never set by
any iteration; every prior decode read only the aggregate return_scores
scalar (iter_006) or align()'s posterior, never the per-step distribution.
what_i_learned:
The aggregate score channel that every whole-hypothesis selector ranks by is
LM-biased toward the fluent-wrong domain spelling (ledger iter_040/041/046),
but the per-STEP logit row still carries the correct domain term as a near-top
competitor at the low-margin fork — information the aggregate folds away. A
raw logit DIFFERENCE equals the log-prob difference (shared log-softmax
denominator), so a margin comparison against the chosen token needs no softmax
and reads the fork free of the cumulative score's LM bias.
hypothesis:
Decode each window once with return_logits_vocab, then snap an emitted content
token to a glossary token when the glossary token's per-step logit is within
2.0 nats below the chosen token's AND decodes to a same-length Hangul surface
(a consonant/vowel substitution, not a length change or inflection). This is
length-preserving (coverage-safe), error-propagation-free (fixed-correct
target), and attacks the dominant substitution axis at the per-step fork the
aggregate-score selectors structurally cannot reach. Glossary is a logit-snap
target set, never a prompt prefix (distinct from cooldown family_006).

capability_investigated:
generate()'s max_initial_timestamp_index decode kwarg — confirmed an accepted
arg by iter_050's TypeError dump but never set by any iteration. After the SOT
prefix Whisper emits a first <|t|> token declaring where the first segment
starts; this kwarg caps how large that initial timestamp index may be.
what_i_learned:
ctranslate2's default lets the initial timestamp run ~1.0s into the window, so
the decoder can mark a window's leading audio as skip-able and delete the
speech there. Because the long-form seek already advances to the previous
window's last timestamp, each new window starts exactly where speech resumed —
so the true first content sits at the window origin and any non-zero initial
timestamp on such a window is a structural deletion. Clamping the index to 0
forces the decode to begin at t=0. This is a WHERE-decode-begins lever,
orthogonal to every WHAT-is-decoded lever (glossary, align, K-best, feature
edits) in the ledger, and the first to target the deletion axis from the
timestamp channel rather than beam length-normalization (iter_047).
hypothesis:
Set max_initial_timestamp_index=0 on a single deterministic beam pass (glossary
cond-B and temperature ladder removed to measure the lever in isolation). On a
batch under-generating on every file (length_ratio 0.91-0.98, deletions 36%),
forcing decode start at the window origin recovers leading-audio deletions; the
only risk direction (over-coverage / leading hallucination) is the direction
the batch has headroom in.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s no_repeat_ngram_size and repetition_penalty decode kwargs — both
confirmed accepted by iter_050's full TypeError signature dump but never set
by any prior iteration. They constrain the beam search INTERNALLY (hard n-gram
ban + per-step emitted-token down-weighting), unlike every prior repetition
handler (zlib compression gate, no_speech_prob gate) which only detects a
collapse after generation and reacts with a temperature re-decode.
what_i_learned:
These are the only two backend levers that act on the repetition/hallucination
axis at search time rather than post-hoc: the champion and iter_048 both spend
a second decode pass rescuing a collapse the constraint could have prevented,
and that rescue is itself an unconstrained search. Trigram-level no-repeat is
the safe granularity for Korean (legit repeats are uni/bigram), so it can ban
hallucination loops without clipping natural speech — a structurally new use
of the surface, untouched by every substitution-axis re-ranker in the ledger.
hypothesis:
Banning repetition inside the beam (no_repeat_ngram_size=3) plus a gentle
repetition_penalty=1.05, on a single deterministic beam pass with the proven
timestamps-on seek and the whole ladder/glossary apparatus removed, will cut
the inserted/substituted runs that the 0.18 hallucination rate and the 8016
repeated_text flag represent — at lower runtime than the multi-pass incumbent.

capability_investigated:
processor(...).input_features along the FRAME (time) axis — the mutable
post-normalization log-mel fed to the encoder verbatim via to_storage_view
(iter_022). Studied temporal spectral CONTRAST (a frame's energy vs its
immediate time neighbours), the one feature dimension every prior input probe
left untouched.
what_i_learned:
Every ledger feature edit is either a mel-bin-axis operation (iter_036 unsharp
across bins, iter_031 ramp, iter_042 warp, iter_022 CMN) or a time-axis LEVEL
shift (iter_035 constant offset). A time-axis unsharp mask
F + alpha*(F - boxsmooth_time(F)) is a structurally distinct lever: it
high-passes along frames, amplifying transient onsets (consonant bursts, stop
releases) relative to the slowly-varying level, and because it lands after
Whisper's per-input-max normalization it is not undone — a buildable transform
numpy-only (cumsum box filter), orthogonal to mel-axis contrast and to every
decode-side re-search of the same smeared spectrogram.
hypothesis:
The 0715 audio smears transients in TIME (codec/jitter/band-limit ringing) as
well as frequency, blurring the onset cues that disambiguate domain-term
substitutions (sub 58% dominant, length_ratio 0.95 healthy). A temporal
unsharp mask (width-5 frames, alpha 0.6) restores those edges before the
encoder sees them, perturbing WHICH spelling is acoustically supported on the
substitution axis. Replaced the temperature-ladder/glossary champion with a
single beam pass over temporally-sharpened features to isolate the lever.

capability_investigated:
The waveform short-time RMS envelope as a SEGMENTATION (boundary-placement)
