signal — the channel iter_043 flagged as coverage-safe but no kept pipeline
ever built — combined with the processor's <=30s zero-pad contract, used to
replace fixed-clock 30s windowing + timestamp-seek entirely rather than to
scale features.
what_i_learned:
Every ledger pipeline (blind 30s, champion seek-to-last, overlap variants)
cuts on a fixed clock, so a domain term straddling a 30s seam is decoded
context-starved on BOTH sides identically on every pass (the substitution
axis) and its trailing fragment is dropped by the seek (the deletion axis).
An envelope-relative silence gate (frame db < p95 - 30dB, runs >= 0.3s) makes
every boundary fall in a real pause, so no chunk cuts a word — and because
every sample lands in exactly one chunk, coverage cannot regress. Splitting at
the LATEST pause in each <=30s span keeps decode-call count ~ the champion's,
so runtime stays in budget; a pause-free span degrades to a 30s hard cut.
hypothesis:
Removing mid-word seams at the segmentation layer attacks BOTH dominant axes
at once (seam-substitution and dropped-fragment deletion) without any
decode-side re-rank, which the score channel's LM bias defeats. A silence-VAD
windowing pipeline with one beam pass per silence-bounded <=30s chunk should
lower both sub and del relative to the fixed-clock champion.

capability_investigated:
The timestamp channel binned to absolute window-relative start times, used to
partition each fixed-hop overlapping window into a committable CENTRAL BAND vs
deferred edges — a windowing scheme, not the seek pointer every prior pass
reduced the <|t|> tokens to.
what_i_learned:
With CHUNK=30s, HOP=20s the per-window central bands [k*HOP+CONTEXT,
(k+1)*HOP+CONTEXT) tile the timeline contiguously (no gap, no double-cover),
so committing only a window's middle 20s — flanked by 5s of run-up on each
side — is coverage-safe by construction while GUARANTEEING every emitted
segment was decoded with >= CONTEXT seconds of bilateral acoustic context.
This defers BOTH edges; ledger iter_032's timestamp-seek defer only ever
released the right edge, leaving the next window's left edge committed cold.
hypothesis:
The dominant substitution mass is confident-but-wrong domain terms locked in
by context-starved window edges. Forbidding edge commits — emitting each
segment only from the window where it sits centrally, with >=5s context on
both sides — should lower substitutions on exactly those forks that no
decode-side re-search of the same fixed spectrogram can reach, at lower
runtime than the champion (one beam pass, no ladder/cond-B).

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses K-best return list (res.sequences_ids ranked) from
a single beam pass, consumed as a per-token CONSENSUS surface (difflib-aligned
majority vote over the N hypotheses' content tokens) rather than as a
whole-sequence ranking. num_hypotheses==beam_size yields all N from one search.
what_i_learned:
Setting num_hypotheses=beam_size returns the full N-best of one beam pass at no
extra decode cost, so the rank>0 hypotheses (which iter_040 showed carry the
correct domain spelling at low-margin forks) are reachable per window for free.
Aligning them to the rank-0 backbone with difflib SequenceMatcher.get_opcodes
makes a per-span UNWEIGHTED majority vote well-defined: confident windows
produce no 'replace' op (all N agree) so are byte-identical to the top beam,
and only genuine forks can flip — a sub-sequence override whole-hypothesis
selection structurally cannot make, and which sidesteps the score channel's
LM bias toward the fluent-wrong spelling because the vote ignores logprob.
hypothesis:
The substitution axis (58%) survives every whole-hypothesis selector because
the LM-biased score keeps the fluent-wrong path ranked first. A strict
majority vote across the beam's N hypotheses can override a single mis-decoded
domain-term span with the correct spelling that the other beam paths hold,
while leaving confident spans and the timestamp seek untouched — lowering
substitution CER without touching coverage or adding decode passes.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_logits_vocab channel (res.logits, per-step full-vocab
logit row along the emitted path, iter_052) composed with the suppress_tokens
hard-ban kwarg (iter_029) — two channels the ledger probed separately but
never built into a correction or combined with each other.
what_i_learned:
The per-step logit row that return_logits_vocab populates makes a free,
per-window substitution-suspect detector: at an emitted CONTENT step (id <
eot) the top1-minus-top2 logit margin is small exactly where the correct
domain term sits just below the chosen fluent-wrong one. Feeding those chosen
ids to suppress_tokens deletes them from the next search, so the beam is
forced onto the next-best acoustic path — a structural escape from the
score channel that every re-ranking selector lacked. The banned-fluent path
legitimately scores lower, so adoption needs a log-prob FLOOR (not a strict
improvement test) plus a compression gate.
hypothesis:
Re-decoding each window once with suppress_tokens set to the low-logit-margin
content forks of the base beam pass should flip confident-but-wrong domain
terms onto the acoustically-supported alternative the ranking buries, lowering
substitution (58% of error mass) while confident windows (no low-margin fork)
stay byte-identical and runtime stays near champion.

capability_investigated:
Why iter_059 crashed: generate()'s return_logits_vocab channel (res.logits)
versus the K-best sequences_ids list. The model runs on cuda/float16, so
res.logits is a GPU-resident StorageView; np.asarray on it dereferences a
NULL host pointer ("data is NULL but array contains data"). Re-targeted the
same substitution-fork signal at sequences_ids[1] (the rank-1 beam).
what_i_learned:
The per-step logit row is NOT convertible to numpy from the workspace: it
lives on the cuda device and there is no SV->host helper in the frozen
surface, so return_logits_vocab is effectively unreachable (np.asarray throws
before any compute). But the SAME fork it would flag is also visible in the
rank-1 beam hypothesis — sequences_ids are plain Python int lists (host-side,
no conversion), so a difflib diff of rank-0 vs rank-1 reads the low-margin
substitution forks (iter_040) with zero GPU dependency.
hypothesis:
On confident (gate-passing) windows — where the confident-but-wrong domain
term hides and cond B never fires (iter_051) — diff rank-0 against rank-1; for
each SHORT replace span (<=3 content tokens, the single-syllable domain
substitution) hard-ban the rank-0 ids via suppress_tokens and re-search once,
adopting under the compression gate plus a log-prob floor. CPU-safe, builds on
best (iter_046) keeping the glossary cond-B path intact, and the span limit
bounds how often the extra beam pass fires so runtime stays near champion.

capability_investigated:
The long-form seek loop's window placement: the champion advances `seek` to
each window's last timestamp and starts the next window exactly there, so
consecutive windows abut with zero overlap and every window's leading content
is decoded at the buffer origin with no preceding audio and no preceding
decoded text. Studied whether the decode buffer can begin BEFORE `seek`
(left run-up) while keeping the emitted span unchanged.
what_i_learned:
Left context for a window's leading content is a coverage-SAFE lever distinct
from every prior windowing scheme: iter_032 deferred only the right edge,
iter_057's central-band gave both edges context but collapsed coverage (len
0.59) by binning/dropping segments. Decoding RUNUP seconds before `seek` and
DISCARDING the run-up tokens (the previous window already emitted that span)
supplies the buffer-origin content with left acoustic + LM context without
ever reducing the emitted span — so length_ratio cannot regress the way a
re-segmentation does, since the run-up is pure context, not a coverage cut.
hypothesis:
The dominant substitution mass is confident-wrong domain-term commits at
context-starved window origins (sub 58%, length_ratio 0.95 healthy). Giving
each window 5s of decoded-then-discarded left run-up lets the decoder resolve
the leading domain term against preceding audio and text instead of cold,
attacking those substitutions structurally rather than re-ranking the same
context-starved features.

capability_investigated:
model.align(features, start, [t0, t1], num_frames).text_token_probs
(iter_021/044) batched over the rank-0 AND rank-1 beam hypotheses of a single
num_hypotheses=beam_size pass (iter_058), used as a per-SPAN acoustic arbiter
rather than a whole-hypothesis re-ranker (iter_023) or an unweighted token
vote (iter_058).
what_i_learned:
rank-1 is the model's own next-best path (host-side int list, iter_060) and
carries the correct domain spelling at low-margin forks (iter_040), but
iter_058's majority vote and every score-channel ranker decide that fork by
an LM-biased signal. align()'s text_token_probs is the missing LM-free
acoustic arbiter (iter_044): restricting swaps to difflib 'replace' spans of
EQUAL token count keeps positions and the interleaved <|t|> timestamps
byte-identical, so the swap is composable with the coverage-safe seek loop
without the re-segmentation that collapsed length_ratio in iter_057/061.
hypothesis:
Decode each window once (N-best), and where rank-0/rank-1 disagree on an
equal-length content span, batch [r0c, r1c] through one align() call and keep
the side with higher summed acoustic posterior — fixing confident-but-wrong
substitutions (sub 58%) at the exact contested syllable, LM-free, with no
external lexicon and zero coverage risk.

capability_investigated:
processor(...).input_features per-mel-bin VARIANCE (second moment over the
time axis) of the normalized log-mel fed to the encoder verbatim via
to_storage_view (mutable, iter_022) — distinct from every prior input probe,
which touched only the first moment (CMN mean iter_022, ramp tilt iter_031,
per-frame lift iter_035) or a fixed geometry (mel/time unsharp local contrast
iter_036/055, VTLP peak relocation iter_042).
what_i_learned:
Each mel bin's std over time is a free per-bin dynamic-range readout on the
already-normalized features, so a data-driven amplify-only gain
clip(target/std, 1, GAIN_MAX) with target=median bin std is a distinct lever
class: it restores the compressed contrast of the 8 kHz transition-band bins
WITHOUT a fixed mel-position assumption (unlike iter_031's ramp), preserves
the per-bin mean (so it is not a level shift), and the [1, cap] clip makes it
amplify-only (a healthy formant bin is left untouched; a noise-floor bin above
the telephone cutoff cannot be blown up). Lands after Whisper per-input-max
normalization so it is not undone.
hypothesis:
The substitution mass (sub 58%, len 0.95 healthy) is band-limit consonant
confusion in low-contrast rolled-off bins; equalizing each bin's variance
toward the median bin's dynamic range restores the consonant detail before the
encoder reads it, perturbing WHICH spelling is acoustically supported —
orthogonal to every decode-side re-search of the same compressed features.
Decode is a single isolated beam pass so the lever is measured alone.

capability_investigated:
processor(...).input_features mel-bin VTLP warp (iter_042) re-used not as a
standalone pipeline but as the SOURCE of a second hypothesis for a correction
layer over the beam5 backbone — i.e. two warped greedy decodes as independent
acoustic witnesses, reconciled by difflib against the strong first-pass beam.
what_i_learned:
A warp relocates each formant peak to a different mel bin, so unlike the
rank-1 beam (iter_062) and K-best vote (iter_058) — which ride the SAME
smeared spectrogram and only see forks the band-limit already made low-margin
— two warps are genuinely independent acoustic views. Restricting overrides to
equal-length, content-only ('t < eot_id'), contiguous-in-backbone spans makes
the interleaved <|t|> timestamps and the long-form seek byte-identical, so the
correction cannot regress length_ratio. This needs no align() call, so it
avoids the GPU-StorageView/arg crash class that killed iter_059/060/061.
hypothesis:
iter_042 lost the beam's quality by running two-warp consensus as the whole
pipeline (cer 0.166); as a high-precision correction layer that fires only
where two relocated-peak witnesses UNANIMOUSLY contradict a strong beam5
backbone, it should fix peak-position domain-term substitutions (the dominant
axis) without touching the windows the backbone already gets right.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch axis as the DUAL of iter_038: N copies of the SAME
bare-SOT prompt paired with N DIFFERENT feature tensors (acoustic-perturbation
ensemble) in one batched launch, rather than iter_038's N different prefixes
on the SAME features. Studied whether the same-position-SOT batch constraint
(iter_039) permits this configuration and what one launch returns.
what_i_learned:
The same-SOT-position constraint that forced iter_038/039's prefix ensemble
apart is satisfied trivially when every batch prompt is identical, so the
features axis is free to differ per entry — a single generate() call can carry
N independent acoustic VIEWS (here VTLP warps, iter_042) of one window at the
cost of N greedy beams ≈ one beam pass. This makes ensemble-of-greedy + per
-token majority vote a runtime-feasible decode strategy distinct from every
beam-centric pipeline: the warps relocate formant peaks so the views are
genuinely independent witnesses (unlike rank-1 iter_062 / K-best iter_058 that
ride the unwarped spectrogram), and voting only on equal-length difflib spans
over the identity-warp backbone leaves timestamps + token count untouched
(coverage-safe, LM-free).
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (58%) because one search over one smeared 8 kHz
spectrogram is committed to; majority-voting N warped greedy decodes per
content-token position lets the band-limited substitution forks be decided by
acoustic agreement across peak-relocated views instead of the LM-biased score
channel, overwriting a backbone token only on a strict 3/5 majority.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s prompt input as a CROSS-WINDOW conditioning surface: the
<|startofprev|> channel fed with the model's OWN previously-decoded window
text (a call-local running prior), composed with the return_scores (iter_006)
and return_no_speech_prob (iter_048) confidence channels used as a gate on
what context is allowed to propagate.
what_i_learned:
Prev-text conditioning was tried once (iter_011) and error-cascaded because it
propagated the running tail unconditionally — one wrong window seeds the next.
The backend exposes everything needed to break that cascade WITHOUT a new
channel: avg_logprob (scores), no_speech_prob, and the zlib compression ratio
are all readable per window, so a window can be barred from becoming the next
window's prior unless it decoded confidently. This makes prev-text a gated,
self-cleaning input rather than the open-loop poison it was in iter_011, and
it is call-adaptive in a way the fixed glossary (family_006) structurally is
not — orthogonal to every feature transform, re-rank, ensemble in the ledger.
hypothesis:
Domain-term substitutions (sub 58%, length healthy) are local: a term blurred
by 8 kHz acoustics at t=400s was usually spelled in context at t=380s. Feeding
the previous confident window's text as a <|startofprev|> prior gives the
decoder that disambiguating local context on every window including the cold
opening, lowering substitution CER, while the confidence gate on propagation
prevents the iter_011 cascade.

capability_investigated:
The finished transcript as a per-call corpus with internal spelling
agreement, decomposed to Hangul jamo (U+AC00 choseong/jungseong/jongseong
arithmetic, pure CPU) against a recurrence-derived canonical set — composing
iter_037's singleton-variant recurrence fact with iter_041's jamo separability,
neither of which was ever built into a kept correction stage.
what_i_learned:
A self-glossary canonical (token freq >= 3, no external list, error-
propagation-free) plus jamo decomposition makes a "same jungseong, interior
syllable only, consonant differs" singleton->canonical rewrite expressible as
a post-decode pass with ZERO extra decode and no backend channel. It reads
the output spelling-frequency distribution, not the return_scores logprob that
is LM-biased toward the fluent-wrong spelling, so it can flip a confident
substitution that every beam-confined re-ranker leaves intact; the interior-
only diff guard (i not in {0, len-1}) structurally protects the final
inflectional particle (보험을/보험은) and the swap is equal-length so
length_ratio is invariant.
hypothesis:
Replacing each rare singleton token with its unique recurring canonical twin
under the same-vowel/interior/particle-protected jamo guard fixes the
consonant-confusion substitutions (dominant axis 58%) the score channel
cannot, without touching coverage or runtime.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s long-form seek loop run from a non-zero start sample offset
(half a chunk), producing a second full-call transcript whose window seams
fall at the centers of the first grid's windows — the temporal-framing
degree of freedom every prior windowing probe (overlap iter_016/026/032,
central-band iter_057, run-up iter_061) left at a single fixed phase.
what_i_learned:
The seek loop is phase-invariant in mechanism but not in output: starting it
at +15s relocates every window boundary, so a span seam-starved under grid A
is decoded with full bilateral context under grid B. The two transcripts are
independently producible and difflib-alignable at character level (mostly-
equal strings, autojunk=False), and grid-A segment lengths recover the exact
seam character offsets — so a witness swap can be confined to seam-local
'replace' spans without touching the strong beam decode elsewhere, making the
reconciliation coverage-safe by construction (grid A defines extent).
hypothesis:
Decode grid A (beam5, authoritative) and a half-chunk phase-shifted grid B
(greedy witness), then overwrite only grid-A 'replace' disagreements within
14 chars of an A-seam with grid B's reading. This rescues the seam-straddling
domain-term substitutions (dominant axis) that no single-grid pass can see,
at ~1.5x the champion's decode cost (greedy witness keeps runtime in budget).

capability_investigated:
Composed two cross-family parents' seek mechanisms: family_004's
penultimate-timestamp window-overlap (emit up to the OPENING timestamp of the
final segment and advance seek there, so that trailing segment is re-decoded
as an interior segment next window) running over family_005's beam_size=5
global-cumulative-logprob first pass instead of greedy.
what_i_learned:
The two parents attack the substitution axis from orthogonal sides and the
weaknesses are complementary: family_005's beam fixes a bad greedy LOCAL
commit but leaves the window's trailing segment context-starved; family_004's
overlap gives that trailing segment full right-context but re-reads it under a
greedy decode that re-inherits the local commit. Running the overlap over the
beam means every segment gets BOTH a global-path decode and at least one
decode where it is not the right edge — the two substitution sources are
removed in one pipeline, and ts_positions[-2] (final-segment opening) is the
exact cut that makes the drop+re-read coverage-safe (advance>=20s bounds it to
<=1.5x windows).
hypothesis:
Decode each window with beam_size=5, then seek to the penultimate timestamp
(final-segment opening) when it is >=20s into the window so the trailing
context-starved segment is re-decoded as an interior segment of the next
window; fall back to the champion last-timestamp seek otherwise. Both
substitution sources (bad greedy commit, right-edge context starvation) are
attacked together while length_ratio is preserved by the bounded overlap.

capability_investigated:
The parent (family_006/iter_046) cond-B glossary branch: a second
<|startofprev|>-primed beam_size=5 decode run on every window where cond A
fails the logprob/compression gate, adopted on a within-margin avg-logprob
comparison (return_scores channel, iter_006). Studied whether that branch
earns its compute on the output, given the ledger's own findings about it.
what_i_learned:
Per ledger iter_046 and iter_051 the cond-B branch is doubly weak: (1) its
firing set is mis-targeted — it only runs when cond A FAILS the gate, but the
dominant error is the confident-but-wrong domain term, which PASSES the gate
(score channel is LM-biased toward the fluent-wrong spelling), so cond B
never fires on the very windows it was built for; and (2) even when it fires,
the same LM bias means the glossary path usually scores below cond A and is
rarely adopted. So removing it changes the output on very few windows while
eliminating a full extra beam_size=5 decode per gate-failing window — an
equal-CER, lower-runtime simplification (the ablation thesis).
hypothesis:
Drop the glossary cond-B mechanism entirely; keep only the beam first pass +
temperature-fallback ladder + long-form seek. If CER holds at ~0.1585 the
simpler, faster pipeline is the win this ABLATE slot asks for; if it
regresses, that quantifies cond-B's true (small) contribution.

capability_investigated:
The processor->encoder input path treated as a NONLINEAR waveform surface: a
full-wave rectification |x| applied to the raw waveform before processor(),
generating sum/difference harmonics, vs every prior input probe which edits
the already-computed mel features with a linear op (CMN iter_022, ramp
iter_031, mel/time unsharp iter_036/055, VTLP bin warp iter_042/064, variance
gain iter_063).
what_i_learned:
A linear mel transform cannot recover the consonant band the 8 kHz telephone
cutoff removed — there is no energy above the rolloff for it to lift or
relocate, so a band-limit substitution survives all of iter_022/031/036/042/
055/063. Nonlinear rectification is a distinct lever CLASS: |x| of a 0.3-3.4
kHz signal has harmonic images extending to ~6.8 kHz, so high-pass-isolating
the rectified ripple (cumsum box filter) and adding it back synthesizes NEW
high-band content correlated with the speech — an acoustic witness that does
not ride the same band-limited spectrogram the warp/rank-1/K-best views all
share.
hypothesis:
Decode the band-extended chunk greedily as an independent witness over a
beam_size=5 backbone, overriding only equal-length content-only difflib
'replace' spans. The reconstructed high band can flip a domain-term
substitution the band-limited beam locked onto, while equal-length spans keep
token count and timestamps byte-identical so coverage/length_ratio cannot
regress.

capability_investigated:
The decode-PROMPT axis composed across the two given parents: family_006
decodes WITH timestamps (the <|t|> tokens are its mandatory long-form seek
channel) and strips them post hoc, while family_001 uses the <|notimestamps|>
prompt for a pure transcription path. I studied whether the committed span's
emitted text can come from the notimestamps path while segmentation still
comes from the timestamp path — two prompt structures over the same window.
what_i_learned:
The seek/segmentation role and the transcription role of a window decode are
separable: once the timestamp pass fixes `advance` (a real segment
boundary), the committed [0, advance] sub-chunk can be re-decoded with the
notimestamps prompt independently, and because advance/seek are reused
verbatim this changes only the emitted CHARACTERS, never the windowing — so
unlike family_001's blind 30s cut (del_ratio 0.796) it cannot slice a word or
regress length_ratio. The notimestamps text was previously never produced by
the champion at all (every committed token path had interleaved <|t|>).
hypothesis:
family_006's emitted text is produced by a path that had to interleave a
timestamp token between segments; re-transcribing the already-segmented span
with family_001's clean notimestamps prompt removes that interference from
the text path while keeping family_006's coverage-safe segmentation, and a
compression gate falls back to the timestamp text when the notimestamps
decode collapses — targeting substitution without touching coverage.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses K-best return list (res.sequences_ids ranked,
with res.scores) consumed as a whole-hypothesis COVERAGE surface — the
decision rule for WHICH of the N-best to commit — rather than rank-0
(length-normalized cumulative logprob) selection or iter_058's per-token
majority vote.
what_i_learned:
Rank-0 is chosen by length-normalized cumulative log-prob, which structurally
prefers shorter paths; the diagnosis confirms this is not per-window noise but
a corpus-wide deficit (length_ratio < 1.0 on all 11 files, 0.91-0.98; deletion
36% of error mass), worst on long-continuous-speech files. The N-best of one
beam pass is free (iter_058) and host-side (iter_060), so a longer near-equal
hypothesis the search already found is reachable per window with no extra
decode and no GPU crash class.
hypothesis:
Select, among one window's N-best, the LONGEST hypothesis whose avg log-prob
stays within _SCORE_MARGIN (0.15 nats) of rank-0 and clears the compression
gate, defaulting to rank-0. This recovers dropped clauses at bounded
confidence cost (margin + compression gate cap the hallucination/repetition
risk the two flagged files carry), attacking the deletion axis from the
selection rule rather than beam length-normalization (iter_047), timestamp
clamp (iter_053), or windowing.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s length_penalty decode kwarg (ct2 beam score =
cumulative_logprob / length**length_penalty, ledger iter_047) applied to
BOTH beam passes of the family_005+family_006 merge — the cond A bare-SOT
beam and the cond B glossary-primed beam.
what_i_learned:
The current pipeline already grafts both given parents (beam_size=5 first
pass + glossary cond-B margin), and both attack only substitution; neither
touches length_penalty, so the deletion axis is unguarded. length_penalty is
an accepted kwarg (iter_050 dump) that acts at search time on every beam
pass at once, the only beam-internal lever for the corpus-wide length deficit
(length_ratio 0.91-0.98 on all 11 files, deletion 36% of error mass).
hypothesis:
Set length_penalty=1.2 on both beam_size=5 decodes so the length normalizer's
exponent lifts longer, more-complete hypotheses relative to short ones. This
composes the substitution-axis merge with a deletion-axis guard the two
parents both omit, addressing the 36% deletion mass without disturbing the
glossary/beam substitution mechanism.

capability_investigated:
Composed the two plateau parents at the pipeline level: family_008's
phase-shifted dual-grid seek (Grid A beam_size=5 from t=0 owns
coverage/segmentation; Grid B greedy beam_size=1 started chunk_len//2 later as
an independent temporal witness) reconciled by difflib opcodes, then
family_007's jamo-decomposition (U+AC00 cho/jung/jong arithmetic) glossary
output corrector — both reached with no new backend channel, only generate()
beam_size + the host-side decoded text.
what_i_learned:
The two parents' substitution fixes target disjoint sources and compose
without conflict: Grid B can only rescue a seam-starved span because the phase
offset relocates it to a window center, while the jamo corrector only fires on
systematic same-every-window consonant confusion both grids share — so the
dual-grid reconcile (seam-local 'replace' only, inserts dropped) leaves
coverage to Grid A's seams and the corrector reads the post-reconcile text, a
clean two-stage ordering. The family_006 cond-B glossary-prompt branch is
dropped (ledger iter_046/051/070), so this slot also measures the
text-glossary against the prompt-glossary on the same beam backbone.
hypothesis:
Grafting the seam witness (substitution-from-context-starvation) and the jamo
glossary corrector (substitution-from-band-limit consonant confusion) into one
pipeline removes two orthogonal substitution sources at once while Grid A
guards length_ratio and dropped Grid-B inserts guard hallucination — attacking
the dominant sub axis from both sides the single-grid champion cannot.

capability_investigated:
family_006's cond-B firing predicate — the threshold deciding WHICH windows
get the glossary-primed <|startofprev|> beam pass. It currently reuses the
acceptance gate's _LOGPROB_THRESHOLD (-1.0), so the cond-B firing set is
identical to the gate-FAILURE set. Studied it as a tunable trigger threshold
distinct from the adoption margin (iter_046) per ledger iter_051.
what_i_learned:
The trigger and the margin are independent levers on the same branch:
iter_046 tuned the avg-logprob adoption margin (which decode wins once cond B
runs), but the SET of windows that ever reach that comparison is fixed by the
trigger. With the trigger pinned at the gate (-1.0), confident-but-wrong
substitutions score above -1.0, PASS the gate, and cond B never fires on them
— the parent paid for cond B yet structurally excluded the dominant-axis
windows. Decoupling the trigger to -0.5 admits the moderate-confidence band
without touching acceptance, and runtime has ~3x headroom (227s vs 720s) for
the extra beam passes.
hypothesis:
Adding _GLOSSARY_TRIGGER_LOGPROB=-0.5 and firing cond B when
lp_a < -0.5 (not < -1.0) exposes the [-1.0,-0.5) substitution-risk windows —
exactly where the glossary correction was designed to act — to the domain
prior, while the unchanged -1.0 acceptance gate and 0.1 adoption margin bound
error-propagation risk. Targets the dominant substitution axis (58%).

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses K-best list (res.sequences_ids + res.scores) from
a single beam pass, consumed under a Minimum-Bayes-Risk WHOLE-hypothesis
selection rule — pick the hypothesis with max total character-level
difflib similarity to every other N-best member (uniform weights) — never
applied in the ledger.
what_i_learned:
The K-best of one beam pass admits a selection rule structurally distinct
from rank-0 logprob, iter_058's per-token majority vote, and iter_073's
longest-hypothesis: MBR ranks each whole hypothesis by its consensus (mean
similarity) with the rest, so with UNIFORM weights the LM-biased score
channel (iter_040/041/046, which favors the fluent-wrong domain spelling)
gets no vote at all — the spelling the independent beams agree on wins. It
needs no extra decode, stays host-side (no GPU StorageView), and the picked
hypothesis keeps its own <|t|> tokens so the long-form seek is unchanged.
hypothesis:
Replacing logprob/gate-based selection with uniform-weight MBR consensus
over the N-best directly attacks the dominant substitution axis: on a
low-margin domain-term fork where rank-0 spelled it fluently-wrong but
ranks 1..4 cluster on the correct term, the consensus pick flips to the
agreed spelling without touching length (so coverage is unrisked).

capability_investigated:
The decode-PROMPT axis across the two plateau parents — family_003's
timestamp-ON seek (the <|t|> tokens fix `advance`/segmentation) and
family_001's <|notimestamps|> pure-transcription prompt re-decoding the
already-committed [0, advance] span. Studied generate()'s notimestamps
output extent vs the timestamp-path text extent as an adoption signal.
what_i_learned:
family_001's notimestamps re-transcription adopts on a bare compression
gate, but a span-fed notimestamps beam has no <|t|> anchoring and can drift:
it over-generates (hallucination/repeat, hal 0.182) or under-generates
(collapse) relative to the timestamp text, and that drift is visible as a
character-count divergence with ZERO extra channel — both texts are already
decoded host-side. So len(nt) vs len(ts) is a free per-window guard that the
compression ratio alone (which only catches the repeat sub-case) misses.
hypothesis:
Graft family_001's notimestamps re-transcription onto family_003's
timestamp-seek backbone, but adopt the clean nt_text only when it both
clears the compression gate AND stays within _NT_LENGTH_BAND (0.15) of the
timestamp text's char count; else keep the coverage-anchored timestamp text.
The length band rejects exactly the over/under-generation that pushed
family_001's hallucination axis up, so the cleaner transcription path lands
only where it agrees in extent with the segmentation-anchored decode.

capability_investigated:
The waveform short-time RMS envelope as a SEGMENTATION (boundary-placement)
signal — ledger iter_056 derived this as coverage-safe but no kept pipeline
ever built it. Computed p95-relative frame dB over 20ms RMS frames directly
from the input audio array (numpy only, no forbidden assets), turned pauses
>=0.3s into cut points, and replaced the fixed-clock 30s seek loop entirely.
what_i_learned:
Boundaries can be placed from the audio array itself rather than from the
decoder's <|t|> seek channel: the p95-relative silence gate is buildable with
numpy alone (frame RMS -> dB -> percentile -> run-length on the silence mask)
and tiles [0,n) contiguously, so coverage is structurally byte-complete while
every cut lands in a real pause. This is the first pipeline whose chunk
boundaries are content-aware instead of clock-aligned; a pause-free span
(longest_speech_s up to 233s in the worst file) degrades to a hard 30s cut,
so VAD only ever changes the windows where a pause actually exists.
hypothesis:
Fixed-clock cuts straddle domain terms at 30s grid lines, decoding them
context-starved on both sides (substitution 58%) and dropping the fragment
(deletion 36%). Cutting at the latest real pause within each <=30s span means
no chunk slices a word, removing both seam error sources by construction
while keeping ~champion decode-call count (runtime in budget).

capability_investigated:
The raw-waveform path into processor() as a PRE-FILTERBANK filtering surface:
applying a first-order pre-emphasis high-pass (y[n] = x[n] - 0.97*x[n-1]) to
the chunk waveform before the log-mel is computed — iter_013 recorded that
Whisper's front end applies no pre-emphasis, but no iteration built it.
what_i_learned:
Every ledger feature edit (CMN, ramp, lift, mel/time unsharp, VTLP, variance
gain) operates on the log-mel AFTER the filterbank has pooled energy, and
iter_071's only waveform op was nonlinear rectification. A linear pre-emphasis
filter is a structurally distinct lever: it changes the energy distribution
BEFORE the filterbank pools and the log compresses, so it reshapes which
in-band (0.3-3.4 kHz) energy reaches each mel bin in a way no post-filterbank
linear op can reproduce — boosting the weak consonant band relative to the
strong vowel band, without trying to synthesize content above the telephone
cutoff (iter_071's nonlinear goal).
hypothesis:
The dominant axis is confident-but-wrong domain terms on band-limited audio
(sub 58%, length_ratio 0.95 healthy), i.e. weak consonant contrast collapsing
similar terms onto one token path. Pre-emphasising the waveform before the
log-mel restores the upper-speech-band tilt the front end omits, so the mel
filterbank delivers stronger consonant cues and the beam can separate the
confusable terms. Rewrote to a clean single beam-pass timestamps-on seek
backbone (glossary cond-B dropped, family_006 cooldown) to measure the
front-end filter in isolation.

capability_investigated:
The interleaved <|t|> timestamp tokens of a window decode used as an INTERNAL
partition for a recursive sub-segment re-decode, rather than as the seek
pointer every windowing probe (overlap, central-band, run-up, phase-shift,
VAD, notimestamps whole-span re-transcribe) reduced them to. Studied whether
generate() can be re-invoked per <|t|>-bounded span of one window using the
return_scores avg-logprob as the gate on which windows pay for it.
what_i_learned:
A window-global beam decode shares one running hypothesis across every speech
segment the 30s window contains, so a confident-but-wrong domain-term commit
early in the window biases the beam state for the remaining segments — a
cross-segment contamination channel no whole-window re-rank, K-best vote, or
feature edit in the ledger can break, because they all re-search the same
single window-global path. The <|t|> tokens already partition the committed
span into per-segment (start,end) times host-side (no GPU StorageView, no
align/logits crash class), so each segment is independently re-decodable as
its own short clip whose beam shares no state with its neighbours.
hypothesis:
On low-confidence windows (avg_logprob < -0.5, the substitution band that
scores above the -1.0 acceptance floor) re-decode each <|t|>-bounded segment
in isolation with a clean <|notimestamps|> prompt and concatenate; isolation
removes the cross-segment beam contamination so a bad commit can no longer
propagate, attacking the dominant substitution axis. Coverage/segmentation
stay on the unchanged seek and adoption is length-band + compression gated,
so deletion/over-generation cannot regress.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses return list consumed in SAMPLING mode
(beam_size=1 + sampling_topk=0 + sampling_temperature>0) rather than beam
mode — whether one call returns N genuinely INDEPENDENT full-distribution
draws of a window, versus the prefix-sharing K-best of a single beam search
that iter_058 (token vote) and iter_077 (MBR) both consumed.
what_i_learned:
Beam K-best (iter_058/077) and feature-warp views (iter_065) are correlated
witnesses: they agree with the chosen path everywhere except forks the beam
already kept open, so they structurally cannot surface a CONFIDENT-but-wrong
commit — the dominant error (sub 58%, len 0.95 healthy). Sampling-mode
num_hypotheses=N is the missing independent-witness source: each draw is a
separate full-distribution sample (host-side int lists, no GPU StorageView /
logits crash class), so an LM-biased fluent-wrong spelling sampled on one
draw is sampled away on another and fails to reach quorum, while the
acoustically-pinned domain term recurs across draws. A strict >=3-of-4
majority agreeing on a span the beam did NOT emit is evidence the beam's
high-confidence commit was LM-over-acoustics.
hypothesis:
Keep a beam_size=5 timestamp pass as the coverage/segmentation backbone
(advance + emit_ids unchanged, so length_ratio cannot regress), then draw N=4
independent samples (temp 0.4) in one extra call and difflib-vote their texts
against the committed beam text: override a 'replace' span only when >=3 of 4
independent draws propose the SAME alternative. This flips confident
substitutions that every prefix-correlated re-ranker leaves intact, while the
strong beam text is the floor wherever the noisy draws fail to reach quorum.
